Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix
$c>0$. All intervals $I,J$ below have nonempty interior. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve
   with $a<b$.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.
   For $a=b$, the unique section is its prescribed fibre vector and
   $P_\gamma$ is the identity; no $D_t$ condition is imposed on a singleton.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ induced by the chart $\psi_p$ on $T_pM$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and let $\exp_q:\mathcal E_q\to M$
be the exponential maps of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. For an open set
$U\subseteq M$ write $T U\subseteq TM$ for the tangent vectors based at
points of $U$.

**(a) Normal neighborhood.** An open neighborhood $U$ of $p\in M$ is a
**normal neighborhood of $p$** when there is an open star-shaped subset
$W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ of $T_pM$ such that $U=\exp_p(W)$ and
$\exp_p|_W:W\to U$ is a diffeomorphism onto $U$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
supplies such pairs). The **exponential coordinates at $p$** on such a $U$
are $u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$ for a linear isomorphism
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$.

**(b) Convex normal and strictly convex normal sets.** An open set
$C\subseteq M$ is **convex normal** when it is a normal neighborhood of each
of its points; thus for every $q\in C$ there is an open star-shaped
$C_q\subseteq\mathcal E_q$ with $\exp_q(C_q)=C$ and
$\exp_q|_{C_q}$ a diffeomorphism onto $C$. It is **strictly convex normal**
when it is convex normal and every pair $q,q'\in\overline C$ is joined by exactly one affinely
parametrized geodesic segment $\gamma:[0,1]\to\overline C$ with
$\gamma(0)=q$ and $\gamma(1)=q'$, and, if $q\ne q'$, its parameter interior
$\gamma((0,1))$ lies in $C$. In the degenerate case $q=q'$, the required
segment is the constant geodesic at $q$; no interior-containment condition
is imposed on this degenerate segment when $q\in\partial C$.

**(c) Position vector.** Fix a normal neighborhood $U=\exp_p(W)$ of $p$
as in (a), with its chosen inverse $(\exp_p|_W)^{-1}$, and let $q\in U$.
Put $v:=(\exp_p|_W)^{-1}(q)\in T_pM$. Since $W$ is star-shaped,
$tv\in W$ for $0\le t\le1$, and
$x(t):=\exp_p(tv)$ is the radial geodesic segment in $U$ from $p$ to $q$.
The vector
$$P(p,q):=\gamma_{p,v}'(1)=d(\exp_p)_{v}(v)\in T_qM$$
is the **position vector of $q$ with respect to $p$**; here
$\gamma_{p,v}$ is the maximal geodesic of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. The notation $P(p,q)$
uses this chosen inverse branch; another normal neighborhood may select a
different radial segment for the same endpoints. On a convex normal set
$C$, use the inverse domains $C_p$ of (b) and the joining segment in $C$;
on a strictly convex normal set this segment is unique by (b).
By the Gauss lemma of
[[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]]
$g_q(P(p,q),P(p,q))=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))$.

**(d) Squared-displacement function.** For a normal neighborhood $U$ of
$p$ the **squared-displacement function** is
$$D_p^2:U\to\mathbb R,\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p\bigl(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q)\bigr).$$
It is smooth on $U$ because $\exp_p^{-1}$ is smooth and $g_p$ is bilinear;
$D_p^2(p)=0$, $D_p^2(q)<0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is timelike,
$D_p^2(q)=0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is null or zero, and $D_p^2(q)>0$
exactly when $P(p,q)$ is spacelike. On a convex normal $C$ we write
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$, $D^2(p,q):=D_p^2(q)$, whenever the position
vector is defined using these inverse domains.

**(e) Scope.** These are definitions inside the smooth Lorentzian model;
they assert no existence of convex normal sets (supplied separately by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), no completeness and no physical
reading. The position vector is an element of $T_qM$, not a vector field and
not a coordinate displacement; $D^2$ is not a metric distance and takes
negative values on timelike-separated pairs.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth and let $p\in M$. The **differential of $F$ at $p$** is the map $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ defined by
$$ dF_p(v)([g]):=v([g\circ F]) $$
for every derivation $v\in T_pM$ and every germ $[g]\in C_{F(p)}^\infty(N)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(\overline{B_s})\times x^{-1}(\overline{B_s})\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map and let $p\in M$. If $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ is
an isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $U$ of $p$ and $V$ of
$F(p)$ such that $F|_U:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

derivations.claim: (Smoothness and the differential in the second argument.) By [L3], $D_p^2$ is smooth on $U_p$. Fix $q\in U_p$, $w\in T_qM$ and a smooth curve $c:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to U_p$ with $c(0)=q$, $c'(0)=w$; put $u(t):=\exp_p^{-1}(c(t))$, so $u$ is smooth and $u'(0)=d(\exp_p^{-1})_q(w)$. Differentiating $D_p^2(c(t))=g_p(u(t),u(t))$ at $t=0$ gives $d(D_p^2)_q(w)=2g_p(u(0),u'(0))=2g_p(v(q),d(\exp_p^{-1})_q(w))$. Since $d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}\circ d(\exp_p^{-1})_q=\mathrm{id}_{T_qM}$, the Gauss lemma [L1] gives $g_p(v(q),d(\exp_p^{-1})_q(w))=g_q\bigl(d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q)),w\bigr)=g_q(P(p,q),w)$. This proves (a).

(Reversal.) Let $v:=v(q)$ and let $\eta(t):=\gamma(1-t)=\exp_p((1-t)v)$ for $t\in[0,1]$. Since $W_p$ is star-shaped, $(1-t)v\in W_p$ and $\eta(t)=\exp_p((1-t)v)$ for $t\in[0,1]$; as $s\mapsto\exp_p(sv)$ is a geodesic and $s=1-t$ is an affine reparametrization with nonzero derivative, $\eta$ is a geodesic with $\eta(0)=q$ and $\eta'(0)=-\gamma'(1)=-P(p,q)$, where $\gamma'(1)=d(\exp_p)_v(v)$. Uniqueness of the maximal initial-value solution implies that $\eta$ is its restriction to $[0,1]$, and in particular $\exp_q(-P(p,q))=\eta(1)=p$. Whenever the chosen normal inverse at $q$ has a domain containing $-P(p,q)$, injectivity of that domain's exponential map gives $\exp_q^{-1}(p)=-P(p,q)$. For that same chosen inverse domain, the reversed segment has terminal tangent $\eta'(1)=-\gamma'(0)=-v(q)$, so $P(q,p)=-v(q)$. If both inverse domains map onto the same strictly convex normal set $C$, the reversed segment stays in $C$; uniqueness in $C$ identifies it with the radial segment selected at $q$, so its initial tangent $-P(p,q)$ belongs to that inverse domain. Finally, by [L1] at base point $p$ with $w=v$, $D_q^2(p)=g_q(\exp_q^{-1}(p),\exp_q^{-1}(p))=g_q(P(p,q),P(p,q))=g_p(v,v)=D_p^2(q)$ under that same inverse-domain condition. This proves (b).

(Differential on pairs.) Let $C$ be strictly convex normal and $p,q\in C$. By [L4] the map $(p',q')\mapsto D^2(p',q')$ is smooth on $C\times C$, and by step 2.1 its values are symmetric, $D^2(p',q')=D^2(q',p')$. Fix $u\in T_pM$ and $w\in T_qM$, choose smooth curves $p(s),q(t)$ in $C$ with $p(0)=p$, $p'(0)=u$, $q(0)=q$, $q'(0)=w$, and put $F(s,t):=D^2(p(s),q(t))=D^2(q(t),p(s))$. By part (a) applied with base point $q(t)$, $\partial_sF(0,t)=d(D^2(q(t),\cdot))_p(u)=2g_p(P(q(t),p),u)$; and by part (a) with base point $p(s)$, $\partial_tF(s,0)=2g_q(P(p(s),q),w)$. The mixed partial derivatives of the smooth function $F$ at $(0,0)$ agree ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]), and $P(q(t),p)\to P(q,p)$ as $t\to0$ by the smoothness of [L4]; hence $dD^2(p,q)(u,w)=\partial_sF(0,0)+\partial_tF(0,0)=2g_p(P(q,p),u)+2g_q(P(p,q),w)$. This proves (c).
Claims (a), (b) and (c) are steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1.

boundaries.reason: Normal neighborhoods contain their base p; the tangent directions and radial segment exist even when q=p.

boundaries.evidence: At q=p the inverse vector and P both vanish, so step 1.1 gives zero differential of D-squared; the reversed vector identities also read zero=zero.
For a single ordered pair (p,q), step 3.1 differentiates in each slot; no larger family of endpoints is needed.

boundaries.reason: The exponential map is a diffeomorphism on the specified star-shaped domain; the formulas make no claim at a conjugate or singular inverse point.

boundaries.evidence: The reversal in step 2.1 uses t and 1-t on [0,1], with the initial and final radial endpoints p and q explicitly exchanged.

boundaries.reason: The proof chooses smooth test curves for finitely many prescribed tangent directions; it does not choose a family indexed by the manifold.
The differential and reversal identities are stated as identities on their common domain, not as an iff claim.
No converse from the displacement identities to existence of a normal neighborhood is asserted.

risk_review.notes: Checked Gauss-lemma differential, radial reversal and pairwise inverse smoothness using the fiber block derivative at every pair. Repaired the arbitrary-normal-branch assertion in b: reversal identities require -P in the chosen inverse domain. Clauses a/c and common convex-normal uses are unchanged; downstream length and inverse-map users cite a/c or common convex normal pairs. Confidence 1.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas. Every compact parameter interval
admits a finite subdivision on each of whose pieces a chart representative
is absolutely continuous. For a continuous curve, the relative neighborhood
formulation and the compact chart-interval formulation of that definition
are equivalent.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into a finite-dimensional
smooth manifold $P$ (in particular $P=\mathbb R$) whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous in charts of $P$ using the same relative neighborhood definition,
and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (with the finite
admissible partition and one-sided endpoint convention of clause (a) of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $F\in AC[a,b]$, then $F'$ exists almost everywhere on $(a,b)$ and belongs to
$L^1[a,b]$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. For $F:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$, the following are equivalent:

1. $F$ is absolutely continuous.
2. $F'$ exists almost everywhere, $F'\in L^1[a,b]$, and
$$F(x)-F(a)=\int_a^xF'(t)\,dt\quad\text{for every }x\in[a,b].$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation
$[f]\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(t)$ on smooth germs at $\gamma(t)$, extending
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] from smooth to $C^1$ curves.
Equal germ representatives agree along the curve near $t$, and the
one-variable product rule proves the derivation identity. In a chart around
$\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** For $k\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$,
a **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization with strictly positive derivative
(including one-sided endpoint derivatives), comparing the increment over the
actual image interval, are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). For $w\in T_pM$ write
$h=h_n$ and $\gamma(w):=-g_p(n,w)$.

1. If $w$ is nonzero future causal, then $\gamma(w)>0$.
2. If $w$ is future unit timelike, then $\gamma(w)\ge1$, with
   $\gamma(w)=1$ if and only if $w=n$, and
   $g_p(h(w),h(w))=\gamma(w)^2-1$.
3. If $w$ is unit timelike, then $w$ is future-directed if and only if
   $g_p(n,w)<0$, and past-directed if and only if $g_p(n,w)>0$; in particular
   $g_p(n,w)\neq0$ for such $w$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), let $p\in M$ and let $U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$
be a normal neighborhood of $p$ with $W_p$ star-shaped, as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ for $q\in U_p$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$, and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))$.

**(a) Differential in the second argument.** $D_p^2$ is smooth on $U_p$ and,
for every $q\in U_p$ and every $w\in T_qM$,
$$d(D_p^2)_q(w)=2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

**(b) Reversal.** Let $q\in U_p$ and let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$,
$\gamma(t)=\exp_p(t\,v(q))$, be the radial geodesic, so that
$\gamma(1)=q$. Then the reversed segment $t\mapsto\gamma(1-t)$ is the
restriction to $[0,1]$ of the maximal geodesic from $q$ with initial velocity
$-P(p,q)$; consequently
$$\exp_q^{-1}(p)=-P(p,q)\quad\text{and}\quad P(q,p)=-\,v(q)=-(\exp_p)^{-1}(q)$$
whenever the chosen normal inverse at $q$ has a domain containing
$-P(p,q)$. This condition holds in particular when both inverses are
those of one strictly convex normal set $C$ containing $p,q$ and the
inverse at $p$ used to define $v(q)$ is the one mapping $C$ to its
radial domain. Merely having $p,q\in C$ does not identify an independently
chosen inverse on $U_p$ with the inverse selected by $C$.
Under the inverse-domain condition, $D_q^2(p)=D_p^2(q)$ by the Gauss
lemma of [[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]].

**(c) Differential on pairs in a strictly convex normal set.** Use the inverse
domains selected by $C$ in this clause. If $C$ is a
strictly convex normal set ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in C$, then
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and for all $u\in T_pM$, $w\in T_qM$,
$$dD^2(p,q)(u,w)=2\,g_p\bigl(P(q,p),u\bigr)+2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas. Every compact parameter interval
admits a finite subdivision on each of whose pieces a chart representative
is absolutely continuous. For a continuous curve, the relative neighborhood
formulation and the compact chart-interval formulation of that definition
are equivalent.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into a finite-dimensional
smooth manifold $P$ (in particular $P=\mathbb R$) whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous in charts of $P$ using the same relative neighborhood definition,
and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (with the finite
admissible partition and one-sided endpoint convention of clause (a) of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. For $F:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$, the following are equivalent:

1. $F$ is absolutely continuous.
2. $F'$ exists almost everywhere, $F'\in L^1[a,b]$, and
$$F(x)-F(a)=\int_a^xF'(t)\,dt\quad\text{for every }x\in[a,b].$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix
$c>0$. All intervals $I,J$ below have nonempty interior. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve
   with $a<b$.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.
   For $a=b$, the unique section is its prescribed fibre vector and
   $P_\gamma$ is the identity; no $D_t$ condition is imposed on a singleton.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $p\in M$.
Let $W_p\subseteq T_pM$ be a star-shaped open neighborhood of $0$ on which
$\exp_p$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open set $U_p:=\exp_p(W_p)$, as supplied
by [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] and
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]; identify
$T_v(T_pM)$ with $T_pM$ for every $v$.

**(a) Gauss lemma.** For every $v\in W_p$ and every $w\in T_pM$,

$$g_{\exp_pv}\bigl(d(\exp_p)_v(v),\,d(\exp_p)_v(w)\bigr)=g_p(v,w).$$

**(b) Radial maximum.** Let $\alpha:[0,1]\to U_p$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike curve with $\alpha(0)=p$, with nonzero future timelike one-sided
tangents, set $q:=\alpha(1)$ and $v_q:=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$. Then

$$L_g(\alpha)\le\sqrt{-g_p(v_q,v_q)},$$

and equality holds if and only if there are $v_0\in W_p$ and a piecewise-$C^1$
strictly increasing surjection $\rho:[0,1]\to[0,\rho(1)]$ with
$v_q=\rho(1)v_0$ and $\alpha(t)=\exp_p(\rho(t)v_0)$ for all $t$; that is,
$\alpha$ is a monotone reparametrization of the radial geodesic segment from
$p$ to $q$. Dividing by $c$, the proper-time increment of $\alpha$ is at most
$\frac1c\sqrt{-g_p(v_q,v_q)}$, which is the proper-time increment of that
radial geodesic.

derivations.claim: (Propagation.) Let $T_0:=\sup\{t\in[t^*,b]:$ for all $s\in[t^*,t]$ one has $\sigma([t^*,s])\subseteq U_p$ and $v(s)$ future timelike$\}$. The set is nonempty and contains a relative right neighborhood of $t^*$ in $[t^*,b]$: $v(t^*)$ is future timelike, future-timelikeness is open in $T_pM$ while $v$ is continuous, and $\sigma([t^*,t])\subseteq U_p$ for $t$ near $t^*$. On $(t^*,T_0)$ define $R=\sqrt{-Q}>0$. By [L5] and [L2] applied with $T:=P(t)$ and $z:=\sigma'(t)$ at every differentiability point with $Q(t)<0$, $g_{\sigma(t)}(P(t),\sigma'(t))\le-R(t)\sqrt{-g(\sigma'(t),\sigma'(t))}$; hence by [L4] $R'(t)\ge\sqrt{-g(\sigma'(t),\sigma'(t))}\ge0$ a.e., so $R$ is nondecreasing on $[t^*,T_0)$ ([[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-absolutely-continuous-functions]]), and $Q=-R^2\le Q(t^*)<0$ there. If $T_0<b$ and $\sigma([t^*,T_0])\subseteq U_p$, then $Q(T_0)=\lim_{t\uparrow T_0}Q(t)\le Q(t^*)<0$ by continuity, so $v(T_0)$ is future timelike and there is $\varepsilon>0$ with $\sigma([t^*,T_0+\varepsilon])\subseteq U_p$ and $v$ future timelike on $[t^*,T_0+\varepsilon]$, contradicting maximality of $T_0$. Hence $T_0=b'$ where $b'=\sup\{t\in[t^*,b]:\sigma([t^*,t])\subseteq U_p\}$, proving (a).

(Derivative formula.) The map $t\mapsto Q(t)$ is the composition of the locally absolutely continuous curve $\sigma$ with the smooth function $D_p^2$, hence is absolutely continuous, and the chain rule at every differentiability point of $\sigma$ gives $\frac{d}{dt}Q(t)=d(D_p^2)_{\sigma(t)}(\sigma'(t))=2g_{\sigma(t)}(P(t),\sigma'(t))$ by [L3]. This proves (c).

(Length inequality.) Let $t^*\le t_1<t_2\le b$ with $\sigma([t_1,t_2])\subseteq U_p$. By step 1.1, $Q<0$ and $R>0$ on $[t_1,t_2]$, and, by the computation of step 1.1, $R'\ge\sqrt{-g(\sigma',\sigma')}$ a.e. on $[t_1,t_2]$. Integrating with [L1] gives $R(t_2)-R(t_1)=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}R'\ge\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\sqrt{-g(\sigma',\sigma')}\,dt=L_g(\sigma|_{[t_1,t_2]})$. This proves (b).
Claims (a), (b), (c) are steps 1.1, 2.1 and 1.2.

boundaries.reason: The given sigma has nonempty [a,b] and a prescribed timelike position at t-star, so the propagation set contains t-star.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 keeps Q(t)<=Q(t-star)<0, so R=sqrt(-Q) stays positive wherever 1/R is used. The derivative d/dt notation does not divide by a time increment.
Statement boundary: When t-star=b, propagation reduces to the supplied timelike endpoint, and clause (b) has no strict pair t_1<t_2 after it.

boundaries.reason: The initial position is explicitly future timelike; a null or zero initial position is outside this monotonicity claim.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 takes a continuous limit at the supremal propagation time and retains Q<0; step 2.1 integrates up to admitted closed endpoints.

boundaries.reason: The propagation supremum is of a nonempty set containing t-star; selecting one test interval requires no countable family of witnesses.
The propagation and length lower bound are conditional inequalities, with no characterization by an iff.
Equality cases of reverse Cauchy-Schwarz quoted in the facts do not constitute a converse assertion of this lemma.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and let $\exp_q:\mathcal E_q\to M$
be the exponential maps of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. For an open set
$U\subseteq M$ write $T U\subseteq TM$ for the tangent vectors based at
points of $U$.

**(a) Normal neighborhood.** An open neighborhood $U$ of $p\in M$ is a
**normal neighborhood of $p$** when there is an open star-shaped subset
$W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ of $T_pM$ such that $U=\exp_p(W)$ and
$\exp_p|_W:W\to U$ is a diffeomorphism onto $U$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
supplies such pairs). The **exponential coordinates at $p$** on such a $U$
are $u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$ for a linear isomorphism
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$.

**(b) Convex normal and strictly convex normal sets.** An open set
$C\subseteq M$ is **convex normal** when it is a normal neighborhood of each
of its points; thus for every $q\in C$ there is an open star-shaped
$C_q\subseteq\mathcal E_q$ with $\exp_q(C_q)=C$ and
$\exp_q|_{C_q}$ a diffeomorphism onto $C$. It is **strictly convex normal**
when it is convex normal and every pair $q,q'\in\overline C$ is joined by exactly one affinely
parametrized geodesic segment $\gamma:[0,1]\to\overline C$ with
$\gamma(0)=q$ and $\gamma(1)=q'$, and, if $q\ne q'$, its parameter interior
$\gamma((0,1))$ lies in $C$. In the degenerate case $q=q'$, the required
segment is the constant geodesic at $q$; no interior-containment condition
is imposed on this degenerate segment when $q\in\partial C$.

**(c) Position vector.** Fix a normal neighborhood $U=\exp_p(W)$ of $p$
as in (a), with its chosen inverse $(\exp_p|_W)^{-1}$, and let $q\in U$.
Put $v:=(\exp_p|_W)^{-1}(q)\in T_pM$. Since $W$ is star-shaped,
$tv\in W$ for $0\le t\le1$, and
$x(t):=\exp_p(tv)$ is the radial geodesic segment in $U$ from $p$ to $q$.
The vector
$$P(p,q):=\gamma_{p,v}'(1)=d(\exp_p)_{v}(v)\in T_qM$$
is the **position vector of $q$ with respect to $p$**; here
$\gamma_{p,v}$ is the maximal geodesic of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. The notation $P(p,q)$
uses this chosen inverse branch; another normal neighborhood may select a
different radial segment for the same endpoints. On a convex normal set
$C$, use the inverse domains $C_p$ of (b) and the joining segment in $C$;
on a strictly convex normal set this segment is unique by (b).
By the Gauss lemma of
[[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]]
$g_q(P(p,q),P(p,q))=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))$.

**(d) Squared-displacement function.** For a normal neighborhood $U$ of
$p$ the **squared-displacement function** is
$$D_p^2:U\to\mathbb R,\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p\bigl(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q)\bigr).$$
It is smooth on $U$ because $\exp_p^{-1}$ is smooth and $g_p$ is bilinear;
$D_p^2(p)=0$, $D_p^2(q)<0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is timelike,
$D_p^2(q)=0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is null or zero, and $D_p^2(q)>0$
exactly when $P(p,q)$ is spacelike. On a convex normal $C$ we write
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$, $D^2(p,q):=D_p^2(q)$, whenever the position
vector is defined using these inverse domains.

**(e) Scope.** These are definitions inside the smooth Lorentzian model;
they assert no existence of convex normal sets (supplied separately by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), no completeness and no physical
reading. The position vector is an element of $T_qM$, not a vector field and
not a coordinate displacement; $D^2$ is not a metric distance and takes
negative values on timelike-separated pairs.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $p\in M$ and let
$U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$ be a normal neighborhood of $p$ as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Let
$\sigma:[a,b]\to U_p$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (locally absolutely continuous,
with future causal nonzero velocity almost everywhere), and write
$$v(t):=\exp_p^{-1}\bigl(\sigma(t)\bigr),\qquad P(t):=d(\exp_p)_{v(t)}(v(t)),\qquad Q(t):=g_p(v(t),v(t))$$
for $t\in[a,b]$. Suppose there is $t^*\in[a,b]$ such that $v(t^*)$ is
future timelike. For any locally absolutely continuous future causal curve
$\eta:[u,v]\to M$, define its Lorentzian length by
$$L_g(\eta):=\int_u^v\sqrt{-g_{\eta(s)}(\eta'(s),\eta'(s))}\,ds,$$
where the derivative is taken almost everywhere and the integral is the
Lebesgue integral. This integral is finite on a compact parameter interval:
the curve image is compact, a finite chart subdivision has bounded metric
coefficients on each piece, and each coordinate derivative is integrable by
local absolute continuity. The radicand is nonnegative almost everywhere by
causality. On piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike curves this agrees with the
length in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Then:

**(a) Propagation.** For every $t\in[t^*,b]$ with
$\sigma([t^*,t])\subseteq U_p$, the vector $v(t)$ is future timelike;
consequently $Q(t)<0$, and $R(t):=\sqrt{-Q(t)}>0$.

**(b) Length inequality.** For all $t^*\le t_1<t_2\le b$ with
$\sigma([t_1,t_2])\subseteq U_p$,
$$R(t_2)-R(t_1)\ \ge\ L_g\bigl(\sigma|_{[t_1,t_2]}\bigr).$$
In particular $R$ is nondecreasing on $[t^*,b]$.

**(c) Derivative formula.** The map $t\mapsto Q(t)$ is absolutely
continuous and
$$\frac{d}{dt}Q(t)=2\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(P(t),\sigma'(t)\bigr)$$
at almost every $t\in[a,b]$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), let $p\in M$ and let $U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$
be a normal neighborhood of $p$ with $W_p$ star-shaped, as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ for $q\in U_p$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$, and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))$.

**(a) Differential in the second argument.** $D_p^2$ is smooth on $U_p$ and,
for every $q\in U_p$ and every $w\in T_qM$,
$$d(D_p^2)_q(w)=2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

**(b) Reversal.** Let $q\in U_p$ and let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$,
$\gamma(t)=\exp_p(t\,v(q))$, be the radial geodesic, so that
$\gamma(1)=q$. Then the reversed segment $t\mapsto\gamma(1-t)$ is the
restriction to $[0,1]$ of the maximal geodesic from $q$ with initial velocity
$-P(p,q)$; consequently
$$\exp_q^{-1}(p)=-P(p,q)\quad\text{and}\quad P(q,p)=-\,v(q)=-(\exp_p)^{-1}(q)$$
whenever the chosen normal inverse at $q$ has a domain containing
$-P(p,q)$. This condition holds in particular when both inverses are
those of one strictly convex normal set $C$ containing $p,q$ and the
inverse at $p$ used to define $v(q)$ is the one mapping $C$ to its
radial domain. Merely having $p,q\in C$ does not identify an independently
chosen inverse on $U_p$ with the inverse selected by $C$.
Under the inverse-domain condition, $D_q^2(p)=D_p^2(q)$ by the Gauss
lemma of [[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]].

**(c) Differential on pairs in a strictly convex normal set.** Use the inverse
domains selected by $C$ in this clause. If $C$ is a
strictly convex normal set ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in C$, then
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and for all $u\in T_pM$, $w\in T_qM$,
$$dD^2(p,q)(u,w)=2\,g_p\bigl(P(q,p),u\bigr)+2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ induced by the chart $\psi_p$ on $T_pM$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis. Write
$v=v^0e_0+v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ for the coordinates of $v$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]) and

$$\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}.$$

Then $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert^2$, and the timelike set
$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$ satisfies

$$T=T_+\cup T_-,\qquad T_+:=\{v:v^0>\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad T_-:=\{v:v^0<-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\}.$$

The sets $T_+$ and $T_-$ are nonempty, disjoint, open in $V$ (for the metric
topology of the distance $d(u,w):=\lVert c(u)-c(w)\rVert_2$ induced by the
coordinates $c(v):=(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$), convex and path-connected, and they are
exactly the two connected components of $T$. In every $\eta$-orthonormal
ordered basis the two displayed coordinate sets coincide with the two
components of $T$ in some order, and they may be interchanged relative to a
previously fixed naming of the components. Moreover

$$\operatorname{cl}(T_+)=\{v:v^0\ge\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{v:v^0\le-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{0\}.$$

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

derivations.claim: (A past point and an appended timelike geodesic.) Let $W_q\subset T_qM$ be the star-shaped domain on which $\exp_q$ maps diffeomorphically onto $C$. Choose a future timelike $w\in W_q$ and then choose $\varepsilon>0$ so small that $-\varepsilon w\in W_q$; this follows from openness of $W_q$ at $0$. Star-shapedness implies $tw\in W_q$ for all $t\in[-\varepsilon,0]$. Thus $\eta(t):=\exp_q(tw)$ lies in $C$ on this interval. Put $q':=\eta(-\varepsilon)$; the segment runs from $q'$ to $q$ with future timelike velocity. Concatenate $\eta$ with the entire future causal curve $\sigma:[0,T_0]\to C$ to obtain a future causal curve $\beta:[-\varepsilon,T_0]\to C$ by [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (d).

(Position vectors with respect to $q'$.) Since $C$ is convex normal and $q'\in C$, the set $C$ is a normal neighborhood of $q'$. At $t^*:=-\varepsilon/2$, the curve $\beta$ lies on the timelike geodesic $\eta$, and $\exp_{q'}^{-1}(\beta(t^*))$ is a positive multiple of the future timelike initial tangent at $q'$ of the segment from $q'$ to $q$. By [[lem-gr-normal-neighborhood-length-monotonicity]] clause (a), applied to $\beta$ based at $q'$, its position vector remains future timelike for every $t\in[t^*,T_0]$, since the whole curve segment stays in $C$. In particular $\exp_{q'}^{-1}(\sigma(s))$ is future timelike for every $s\in[0,T_0]$.

(Limit to $q$.) Fix $s\in(0,T_0]$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, step 1.2 gives that $v_\varepsilon:=\exp_{q'(\varepsilon)}^{-1}(\sigma(s))$ is future timelike, where $q'(\varepsilon)=\exp_q(-\varepsilon w)$. The pairs $(q'(\varepsilon),\sigma(s))$ converge to $(q,\sigma(s))$ in $C\times C$. By [L3] the inverse vectors converge to $\exp_q^{-1}(\sigma(s))$. The future causal cone together with zero is closed, so this limit is future causal or zero. This proves the first claim for every $s\in(0,T_0]$.

(Nonvanishing near the initial point.) By [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] there is an adapted chart around $q$ in which the time coordinate is strictly increasing along every future causal curve contained in the chart. Choose $\delta\in(0,T_0]$ so that $\sigma([0,\delta])$ lies in this chart. Then $x^0(\sigma(s))>x^0(q)$ for every $s\in(0,\delta]$, so $\sigma(s)\ne q$ and $\exp_q^{-1}(\sigma(s))\ne0$. This proves the second claim without inferring that a return at one time makes the entire preceding curve constant.
Steps 2.1 and 3.1 prove the claim.

boundaries.reason: The conclusion delta in (0,T_0] requires a positive-duration causal segment; there is no empty initial time interval in the supplied curve.

boundaries.evidence: The initial position at s=0 is zero; the claim separates positive s, and step 3.1 uses nonconstancy to rule out return to the vertex.

boundaries.reason: The base q and one given curve are fixed; no cardinality parameter occurs in the initial-cone assertion.
The strictly convex normal set supplies a nonsingular exponential inverse; a degenerate metric or exponential inverse is not admitted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and let $\exp_q:\mathcal E_q\to M$
be the exponential maps of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. For an open set
$U\subseteq M$ write $T U\subseteq TM$ for the tangent vectors based at
points of $U$.

**(a) Normal neighborhood.** An open neighborhood $U$ of $p\in M$ is a
**normal neighborhood of $p$** when there is an open star-shaped subset
$W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ of $T_pM$ such that $U=\exp_p(W)$ and
$\exp_p|_W:W\to U$ is a diffeomorphism onto $U$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
supplies such pairs). The **exponential coordinates at $p$** on such a $U$
are $u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$ for a linear isomorphism
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$.

**(b) Convex normal and strictly convex normal sets.** An open set
$C\subseteq M$ is **convex normal** when it is a normal neighborhood of each
of its points; thus for every $q\in C$ there is an open star-shaped
$C_q\subseteq\mathcal E_q$ with $\exp_q(C_q)=C$ and
$\exp_q|_{C_q}$ a diffeomorphism onto $C$. It is **strictly convex normal**
when it is convex normal and every pair $q,q'\in\overline C$ is joined by exactly one affinely
parametrized geodesic segment $\gamma:[0,1]\to\overline C$ with
$\gamma(0)=q$ and $\gamma(1)=q'$, and, if $q\ne q'$, its parameter interior
$\gamma((0,1))$ lies in $C$. In the degenerate case $q=q'$, the required
segment is the constant geodesic at $q$; no interior-containment condition
is imposed on this degenerate segment when $q\in\partial C$.

**(c) Position vector.** Fix a normal neighborhood $U=\exp_p(W)$ of $p$
as in (a), with its chosen inverse $(\exp_p|_W)^{-1}$, and let $q\in U$.
Put $v:=(\exp_p|_W)^{-1}(q)\in T_pM$. Since $W$ is star-shaped,
$tv\in W$ for $0\le t\le1$, and
$x(t):=\exp_p(tv)$ is the radial geodesic segment in $U$ from $p$ to $q$.
The vector
$$P(p,q):=\gamma_{p,v}'(1)=d(\exp_p)_{v}(v)\in T_qM$$
is the **position vector of $q$ with respect to $p$**; here
$\gamma_{p,v}$ is the maximal geodesic of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. The notation $P(p,q)$
uses this chosen inverse branch; another normal neighborhood may select a
different radial segment for the same endpoints. On a convex normal set
$C$, use the inverse domains $C_p$ of (b) and the joining segment in $C$;
on a strictly convex normal set this segment is unique by (b).
By the Gauss lemma of
[[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]]
$g_q(P(p,q),P(p,q))=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))$.

**(d) Squared-displacement function.** For a normal neighborhood $U$ of
$p$ the **squared-displacement function** is
$$D_p^2:U\to\mathbb R,\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p\bigl(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q)\bigr).$$
It is smooth on $U$ because $\exp_p^{-1}$ is smooth and $g_p$ is bilinear;
$D_p^2(p)=0$, $D_p^2(q)<0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is timelike,
$D_p^2(q)=0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is null or zero, and $D_p^2(q)>0$
exactly when $P(p,q)$ is spacelike. On a convex normal $C$ we write
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$, $D^2(p,q):=D_p^2(q)$, whenever the position
vector is defined using these inverse domains.

**(e) Scope.** These are definitions inside the smooth Lorentzian model;
they assert no existence of convex normal sets (supplied separately by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), no completeness and no physical
reading. The position vector is an element of $T_qM$, not a vector field and
not a coordinate displacement; $D^2$ is not a metric distance and takes
negative values on timelike-separated pairs.
