about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the
relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] and the future and past sets of
[[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]]. Then:

**(a) Openness.** For every $x\in M$ the chronological future $I^+(x)$ and
the chronological past $I^-(x)$ are open subsets of $M$.

**(b) The chronological relation is open.** The set
$$\{(x,y)\in M\times M:\ x\ll y\}$$
is open in the product topology of $M\times M$.

**(c) Closure of future and past sets.** Let $F\subseteq M$ be a future set,
that is $I^+(F)\subseteq F$. Then every $q\in\overline F$ satisfies
$I^+(q)\subseteq F$. Dually, if $P$ is a past set ($I^-(P)\subseteq P$) and
$q\in\overline P$, then $I^-(q)\subseteq P$.

For the absolutely continuous curve conclusion (c), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the cited causal-curve calculus and fundamental theorem. The other clauses use the given smooth observer structure, pointwise adapted-chart existence and finite compactness arguments, without these additional curve-calculus premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

derivations.claim: (No closed causal curve.) Let $\delta:[0,1]\to M$ be a future causal curve with $\delta(0)=\delta(1)$, nonconstant. Define the periodic extension $\beta:\mathbb R\to M$ by $\beta(t):=\delta(t-\lfloor t\rfloor)$. On each interval $(n,n+1)$ the curve $\beta$ is the restriction of $\delta$ up to an increasing affine reparametrization, so it is locally absolutely continuous with future causal velocity almost everywhere, and by [L5] this persists across the finitely many junctions of every compact interval: $\beta$ is a future causal curve. It is future-inextendible: if $\beta(t)\to z$ as $t\to+\infty$, then for every $s\in(0,1)$ the sequence $\beta(s+n)=\beta(s)$ converges to $z$, so $\beta(s)=z$ for all $s\in(0,1)$, contradicting the nonconstancy of $\delta$ on $[0,1]$; the same argument at $-\infty$ (using $\beta(s-n)=\beta(s)$) gives past-inextendibility. boundaries.reason: The Cauchy condition on a nonempty spacetime forces S nonempty since the maximal timelike geodesic through any point must meet it.

boundaries.evidence: The local graph includes z=0 and phi(0)=0. The radius parameters a,rho,eta in step 1.2 are strictly positive.
The Cauchy condition counts exactly one parameter visit; step 1.1 excludes a periodic causal loop because repeated visits would violate that count.

boundaries.reason: The conclusion is a topological hypersurface; no smoothness of an arbitrary Cauchy set is assumed.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.2 places the bounding points strictly within the chosen cylinder, and extends their vertical segment inextendibly to enforce a Cauchy intersection.

boundaries.reason: The local graph point is uniquely determined on each vertical line, so its definition needs no nonunique pointwise choice.

boundaries.evidence: The membership phrase x in I-plus(S) iff some S point precedes x is the existential definition used in step 2.1.
Statement boundary: Conversely the same preceding-point witness places x in I-plus(S); the Cauchy decomposition makes the three regions pairwise disjoint.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

We also use the following arclength parametrization fact. For any future
causal curve $\beta:[r_0,r_1]\to M$ with $r_0<r_1$, put
$L:=\ell_h(\beta)>0$, using the locally absolutely continuous length
convention of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. There is an
increasing absolutely continuous bijection
$\theta:[0,L]\to[r_0,r_1]$ such that
$\widetilde\beta:=\beta\circ\theta$ is future causal and
$\ell_h(\widetilde\beta|_{[u,v]})=v-u$ for $0\le u\le v\le L$. A proof is
included in Step 1.2.

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), restricted to a coordinate ball whose closure is compactly contained in a larger adapted chart with the same cone bounds, with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for all sufficiently large $k$ for each fixed integer $n\ge1$ (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas. Every compact parameter interval
admits a finite subdivision on each of whose pieces a chart representative
is absolutely continuous. For a continuous curve, the relative neighborhood
formulation and the compact chart-interval formulation of that definition
are equivalent.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into a finite-dimensional
smooth manifold $P$ (in particular $P=\mathbb R$) whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous in charts of $P$ using the same relative neighborhood definition,
and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (with the finite
admissible partition and one-sided endpoint convention of clause (a) of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a continuous map,
where $I$ has its relative topology. A **chart representative** on a parameter
neighborhood $J\subseteq I$ is $x\circ\gamma|_J$, where $(U,x)$ is a smooth
chart and $\gamma(J)\subseteq U$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for each $t\in I$ there are
$\delta>0$ and a chart $(U,x)$ such that
$\gamma(I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta))\subseteq U$ and every coordinate of
$x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of
$I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta)$ in the sense of
[[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]. This includes one-sided neighborhoods
at included endpoints. Equivalently, for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the coordinates of $x\circ\gamma$ are
absolutely continuous on $[a,b]$. The equivalence and independence of the
chart and smooth atlas are proved in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]]
clause (a); continuity is part of both formulations.

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point: a
constant chart representative has derivative zero everywhere in its interior,
contradicting the full-measure nonzero-velocity requirement.

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ q\in J^+(p)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point: a
constant chart representative has derivative zero everywhere in its interior,
contradicting the full-measure nonzero-velocity requirement.

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ q\in J^+(p)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).
Call a map $x:I\to M$ a **geodesically connectible continuous causal curve**
when it is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and for every strictly convex
normal ball $C$ as produced by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]
([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b)) and all
$t_1<t_2$ in $I$ with $x([t_1,t_2])\subseteq C$, the endpoints $x(t_1)$ and
$x(t_2)$ are joined by a future causal geodesic whose image is contained in
$C$. Write $\le$ for the causal relation of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (defined by locally absolutely
continuous future causal curves) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat .$$

**(a) Absolutely continuous implies connectible.** Every future causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve.

**(b) Connectible curves give causal relations.** Let $x:I\to M$ be a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve and let $t_1<t_2$ in $I$.
If $x|_{[t_1,t_2]}$ is nonconstant, then for every open neighborhood $W$ of
$x([t_1,t_2])$ there is a piecewise smooth future causal curve
$\eta:[t_1,t_2]\to W$ with $\eta(t_1)=x(t_1)$ and $\eta(t_2)=x(t_2)$; in
particular $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$. If the restriction is constant, its endpoints
coincide and reflexivity gives $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$ without asserting a curve
in the nonconstant future causal class.

**(c) Equality of relations.** For $p,q\in M$ the following are equivalent:
$p\le q$; $p=q$ or there is a geodesically connectible continuous causal
curve with endpoints $p,q$.

**(d) One-sided extension.** Let $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a
future-inextendible future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d). Then there is an
inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^*:I^*\to M$ with
$[0,\infty)\subseteq I^*\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\gamma^*|_{[0,\infty)}=\gamma$;
that is, $\gamma$ is contained in a curve that is both future- and
past-inextendible. The dual statement holds for past-inextendible curves.

No choice principle beyond the stated assumptions is used. The extension in (d) is not asserted to be
unique.

On a connected Riemannian manifold define $d_g(p,q)=\inf\{L_g(\gamma):\gamma\text{ is piecewise }C^1\text{ from }p\text{ to }q\}$.

Lengths are those of [[def-riemannian-speed-and-length]]. For each pair $p,q$, [[lem-any-two-points-in-a-connected-smooth-manifold-can-be-joined-by-a-piecewise-c-one-curve]] supplies a curve, so the set of lengths is nonempty, contains a finite real number and is bounded below by zero. Applying the least-upper-bound property [[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]] to the negatives gives a finite nonnegative infimum. On the empty connected manifold this defines the empty distance function; there are no pairs to evaluate. No minimizing curve is part of this definition.
$d_g$ is a finite metric on a connected Riemannian manifold.
The topology of $d_g$ is the manifold topology on every connected Riemannian manifold.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous curve calculus and its fundamental theorem. Use the locally absolutely continuous Riemannian length of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a strongly causal time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(b)) and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite metric on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then for every compact set
$K\subseteq M$ there is $L(K)\in[0,\infty)$ such that
$$\ell_h(\gamma)\le L(K)$$
for every future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with $\gamma([a,b])\subseteq K$.

Consequently, if $\gamma$ is parametrized by $h$-arclength
($\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=t-s$) and its image is contained in the compact set
$K$, then $b-a\le L(K)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(B,d)$ be a compact metric space
([[def-metric-space]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior, let $K\ge0$ be real, and let $\sigma_m:I\to B$,
$m\in\mathbb N$, be $K$-Lipschitz maps,
$d(\sigma_m(s),\sigma_m(t))\le K|s-t|$ for all $s,t\in I$. Then there are a
strictly increasing sequence $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ and a $K$-Lipschitz map
$\sigma:I\to B$ such that $\sigma_{m_j}\to\sigma$ uniformly on every compact
subinterval of $I$.

For the absolutely continuous curve conclusion (c), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the cited causal-curve calculus and fundamental theorem. The other clauses use the given smooth observer structure, pointwise adapted-chart existence and finite compactness arguments, without these additional curve-calculus premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

For each connected component $M_0\subseteq M$ and smooth Riemannian metric
$H$, let $d_H$ denote the Riemannian distance of $H|_{M_0}$. For the following absolutely continuous length assertion, also assume
Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), as required by the cited
fundamental theorem. For any locally
absolutely continuous curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M_0$, use the length
$$\ell_H(\gamma):=\int_a^b\sqrt{H_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt,$$
with the Lebesgue integral and almost-everywhere derivative. This extends the
piecewise-$C^1$ length of [[def-riemannian-speed-and-length]]. The distance
from [[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]] satisfies
$d_H(\gamma(a),\gamma(b))\le\ell_H(\gamma)$; the proof is included below.

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],
[[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]).

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of
$M_0$ that is closed in $M_0$ and bounded in $d_{h'}$ is compact, and every
closed ball $\{q\in M_0:d_{h'}(q,p)\le r\}$ is compact.

For a compact set $K$ contained in one coordinate chart of an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold, there are $0<c\le C<\infty$ such that $c|v|^2\le g_x(v,v)\le C|v|^2$ for $x\in K$. The dimension-zero assertion is vacuous.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

For each connected component $M_0\subseteq M$ and smooth Riemannian metric
$H$, let $d_H$ denote the Riemannian distance of $H|_{M_0}$. For the following absolutely continuous length assertion, also assume
Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), as required by the cited
fundamental theorem. For any locally
absolutely continuous curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M_0$, use the length
$$\ell_H(\gamma):=\int_a^b\sqrt{H_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt,$$
with the Lebesgue integral and almost-everywhere derivative. This extends the

from [[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]] satisfies
$d_H(\gamma(a),\gamma(b))\le\ell_H(\gamma)$; the proof is included below.

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of

derivations.claim: (Common-domain reparametrization in the bounded positive case.) Suppose $0<b<\infty$. Define $\widetilde\alpha_k(t):=\alpha_k\!\left(\frac{b_k}{b}t\right),\qquad 0\le t\le b.$ Since $b_k/b\to1$, after discarding finitely many terms these curves are 2-Lipschitz for $d_h$: the arclength parametrization gives $d_h(\widetilde\alpha_k(s),\widetilde\alpha_k(t)) \le\ell_h(\widetilde\alpha_k|_{[s,t]}) =\frac{b_k}{b}|t-s|\le2|t-s|.$ Their initial points converge to $x$, and their images lie in one closed $h$-ball about $x$ of radius $2b+1$, which is compact by [L4]. Applying [L6] gives a subsequence converging uniformly on $[0,b]$ to a 2-Lipschitz map $\alpha$. The sharper inequality $d_h(\widetilde\alpha_k(s),\widetilde\alpha_k(t)) \le\frac{b_k}{b}|t-s|$ and $b_k/b\to1$ imply $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$. Uniform convergence at the endpoints gives $\alpha(0)=x$ and $\alpha(b)=z$.

(The limit is future causal.) Let $[s,t]$ be a parameter interval such that $\alpha([s,t])$ lies in a strictly convex normal set $C$. Since this image is compact and $C$ is open, uniform convergence implies $\widetilde\alpha_k([s,t])\subset C$ for all sufficiently large $k$. By [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]] clause (a), each approximating causal subarc has a future-causal position vector $w_k=\exp_{\widetilde\alpha_k(s)}^{-1} (\widetilde\alpha_k(t)).$ Smoothness of the two-point inverse on $C\times C$ gives $w_k\to w=\exp_{\alpha(s)}^{-1}(\alpha(t))$; closedness of the future cone gives that $w$ is future causal or zero. Thus $\alpha$ is geodesically connectible. It is locally Lipschitz in charts by its $d_h$-Lipschitz bound and [L7], hence locally absolutely continuous. At almost every differentiability parameter $t<b$, choose a relatively compact adapted chart $U$ around $\alpha(t)$ and $h_0>0$ so $\alpha([t,t+h])\subset U$ for $0<h\le h_0$. For all sufficiently large $k$ the approximating arcs also lie in $U$ and have $h$-length $(b_k/b)h$. By [L7], $\frac{b_k}{b}h\le C\bigl(x^0(\widetilde\alpha_k(t+h)) -x^0(\widetilde\alpha_k(t))\bigr)$ for a chart constant $C$. Passing to the limit and using $b_k/b\to1$ gives $x^0(\alpha(t+h))-x^0(\alpha(t))\ge h/C.$ At differentiability points this yields $(x^0\circ\alpha)'(t)\ge1/C>0$. For small $h>0$ the position vector $\exp_{\alpha(t)}^{-1}(\alpha(t+h))$ is future causal or zero by the preceding connectibility argument; divided by $h$ it tends in coordinates to $\alpha'(t)$, because the differential of the second-variable inverse at the diagonal is the identity ([[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clauses (b),(c)). The future cone is closed and $\alpha'$ has positive time component, so $\alpha'(t)$ is nonzero future causal almost everywhere. This proves $\alpha$ is a future causal curve and is not constant on any nondegenerate interval.

(The future tail in the unbounded case.) Suppose $b=\infty$. For each fixed $T>0$, $[0,T]$ is contained in $[0,b_k]$ for all large $k$. Applying clause (b) of [L1] by diagonal extraction over integer $T$ gives a subsequence converging uniformly on every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ to a future-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$.

(The past tail in the unbounded case.) Define $\delta_k(s):=\alpha_k(b_k+s)$ on $[-b_k,0]$. For each fixed $T>0$, $[-T,0]$ lies in $[-b_k,0]$ for all large $k$. Apply the time-reversed half-line result of [L1] and diagonalize to obtain a past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with $\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that $\delta_k$ converges uniformly to $\alpha^-$ on compact subintervals. A nested subsequence retains both tail limits.

(The zero-length case.) If $b=0$, then $d_h(x,z)\le d_h(x,\alpha_k(0)) +d_h(\alpha_k(0),\alpha_k(b_k)) +d_h(\alpha_k(b_k),z)\le o(1)+b_k+o(1),$ so $x=z$. For every $t\in[0,b_k]$, $d_h(\alpha_k(t),x)\le d_h(\alpha_k(0),x)+t\le o(1)+b_k.$ Hence the curves converge uniformly on their varying domains to the constant curve at $x$.
(Imprisonment.) If the spacetime is strongly causal and all images lie in a compact $K$, [L5] gives $b_k\le L(K)$ for every $k$. Taking limits yields $b\le L(K)<\infty$, excluding the unbounded case.

(The closure relation.) Fix $t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$. For all sufficiently large $k$, $t_+\le b_k+t_-$, so by [L2], $\alpha_k(t_+)\le\alpha_k(b_k+t_-)=\delta_k(t_-).$ The uniform-on-compact limits in steps 1.3-1.4 give endpoints converging respectively to $\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $\alpha^-(t_-)$. This is the stated sequential closure relation.

(Coincident endpoints.) If $x=z$ and $0<b<\infty$, step 1.2 gives a future causal curve $\alpha$ from $x$ to $x$ which is nonconstant on every nondegenerate interval. If $x=z$ and $b=\infty$, concatenate $\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ at their common endpoint $x$. The concatenation is future causal by [L3], and is past- and future-inextendible because its respective tails are; hence it is inextendible.
(Conclusion.) Clause (i) for $b>0$ is steps 1.1-1.2 and for $b=0$ is step 1.5; clause (ii) is steps 1.3, 1.4 and 2.1; clause (iii) is step 2.2; and clause (iv) is step 1.6.

boundaries.reason: The original domains [0,b_k] are nonempty with b_k>0; both converging endpoint sequences are prescribed.

boundaries.evidence: Statement boundary: The bounded limit b=0 is explicitly included: endpoints coincide and the limit is the constant map at x. It is not treated as a positive-duration causal curve.
Statement boundary: Clause (iii) separates coincident endpoints x=z: for b>0 the limit is nonconstant and closed; for b=0 it is constant.
Statement boundary: Unbounded b produces two one-sided inextendible limits, while the degenerate zero-duration alternative is handled in the bounded branch.
Statement boundary: The bounded branch includes the limiting final endpoint z, and the unbounded branch shifts past parameters by b_k to retain that endpoint.
Statement boundary: The successive compact-interval extractions use the declared Countable/Dependent Choice assumptions; they operate on prescribed arclength curves.

boundaries.reason: The four clauses are alternatives and consequences classified by b, not a biconditional characterizing uniform convergence.
No converse reconstructs an original sequence of arclength curves from two proposed inextendible limits.

risk_review.notes: Checked positive bounded reparametrization b_k/b and compact range, cone limit with positive time derivative, separate b=0 constant map, nested future/past half-line limits and event-pair sequential closure. Coincident endpoints and imprisonment use the appropriate alternatives; AC_omega/DC explicit. Reader zero-domain and typing repairs accepted.

citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).
Call a map $x:I\to M$ a **geodesically connectible continuous causal curve**
when it is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and for every strictly convex
normal ball $C$ as produced by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]
([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b)) and all
$t_1<t_2$ in $I$ with $x([t_1,t_2])\subseteq C$, the endpoints $x(t_1)$ and
$x(t_2)$ are joined by a future causal geodesic whose image is contained in
$C$. Write $\le$ for the causal relation of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (defined by locally absolutely
continuous future causal curves) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat .$$

**(a) Absolutely continuous implies connectible.** Every future causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve.

**(b) Connectible curves give causal relations.** Let $x:I\to M$ be a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve and let $t_1<t_2$ in $I$.
If $x|_{[t_1,t_2]}$ is nonconstant, then for every open neighborhood $W$ of
$x([t_1,t_2])$ there is a piecewise smooth future causal curve
$\eta:[t_1,t_2]\to W$ with $\eta(t_1)=x(t_1)$ and $\eta(t_2)=x(t_2)$; in
particular $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$. If the restriction is constant, its endpoints
coincide and reflexivity gives $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$ without asserting a curve
in the nonconstant future causal class.

**(c) Equality of relations.** For $p,q\in M$ the following are equivalent:
$p\le q$; $p=q$ or there is a geodesically connectible continuous causal
curve with endpoints $p,q$.

**(d) One-sided extension.** Let $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a
future-inextendible future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d). Then there is an
inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^*:I^*\to M$ with
$[0,\infty)\subseteq I^*\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\gamma^*|_{[0,\infty)}=\gamma$;
that is, $\gamma$ is contained in a curve that is both future- and
past-inextendible. The dual statement holds for past-inextendible curves.

No choice principle beyond the stated assumptions is used. The extension in (d) is not asserted to be
unique.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $h$ denote the complete conformally rescaled metric $h\prime$ constructed in [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] clause (b). All distances here are within a connected component; each component is complete and its closed $d_h$-bounded sets are compact by clauses (c) and (d). Endpoint convergence puts the joining curves in the component of $x$ for all sufficiently large $k$, since components of a manifold are open. Let
$$\alpha_k:[0,b_k]\to M,\qquad 0<b_k<\infty,$$
be future causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]])
parametrized by $h$-arclength, $\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for
$0\le s\le t\le b_k$, with $\alpha_k(0)\to x\in M$ and
$\alpha_k(b_k)\to z\in M$. Passing to a subsequence, let
$b:=\lim_kb_k\in[0,\infty]$. Then:

**(i) Bounded case.** If $0<b<\infty$, there is a subsequence and a future
causal curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $\alpha(b)=z$ and
$d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ for $s\le t$, such that the subsequence
converges to $\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,b]$ after the following
common-domain reparametrization when $b>0$:
$$\widetilde\alpha_k(t):=\alpha_k\!\left(\frac{b_k}{b}t\right),\qquad 0\le t\le b.$$
Thus $\widetilde\alpha_k(0)=\alpha_k(0)$ and
$\widetilde\alpha_k(b)=\alpha_k(b_k)$. If $b=0$, then $x=z$ and the curves
converge to the constant map at $x$ uniformly on their varying domains in
the sense that $\sup_{0\le t\le b_k}d_h(\alpha_k(t),x)\to0$. The constant
map is the continuous limit, not a future causal curve in the nonzero-velocity
curve class.

**(ii) Unbounded case.** If $b=\infty$, there are a future-inextendible future
causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and a
past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with
$\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that a subsequence converges to $\alpha^+$ uniformly on
every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ and to $\alpha^-$ uniformly on every
compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ (where $\alpha^-$ is the limit of the
curves $s\mapsto\alpha_k(b_k+s)$, $s\le0$, for large $k$). Moreover, for all
$t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$ there are event pairs $u_k,v_k\in M$ with
$u_k\le v_k$, $u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$. Thus
$(\alpha^+(t_+),\alpha^-(t_-))$ lies in the sequential closure of the causal
relation, meaning precisely that it is a limit of pairs in the relation
$\le$.

**(iii) Coincident endpoints.** If $x=z$, then in case (i) with $b>0$ the
curve $\alpha$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $x$
($\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$), and in case (ii) the concatenation $\gamma$ of
$\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ is an inextendible future causal curve
$\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.

**(iv) Imprisonment.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be strongly causal
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b)) and
suppose all images $\alpha_k([0,b_k])$ are contained in one compact set $K$.
Then $b\le L(K)<\infty$ where $L(K)$ is the length bound of
[[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; in particular the case
$b=\infty$ is excluded.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

We also use the following arclength parametrization fact. For any future
causal curve $\beta:[r_0,r_1]\to M$ with $r_0<r_1$, put
$L:=\ell_h(\beta)>0$, using the locally absolutely continuous length
convention of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. There is an
increasing absolutely continuous bijection
$\theta:[0,L]\to[r_0,r_1]$ such that
$\widetilde\beta:=\beta\circ\theta$ is future causal and
$\ell_h(\widetilde\beta|_{[u,v]})=v-u$ for $0\le u\le v\le L$. A proof is
included in Step 1.2.

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), restricted to a coordinate ball whose closure is compactly contained in a larger adapted chart with the same cone bounds, with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for all sufficiently large $k$ for each fixed integer $n\ge1$ (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle beyond the stated assumptions is used.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas. Every compact parameter interval
admits a finite subdivision on each of whose pieces a chart representative
is absolutely continuous. For a continuous curve, the relative neighborhood
formulation and the compact chart-interval formulation of that definition
are equivalent.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into a finite-dimensional
smooth manifold $P$ (in particular $P=\mathbb R$) whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous in charts of $P$ using the same relative neighborhood definition,
and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (with the finite
admissible partition and one-sided endpoint convention of clause (a) of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous from the manifold topology to the usual topology of
$\mathbb R$: for every $p\in M$ and every open neighborhood $W$ of $u(p)$
there is an open neighborhood $V$ of $p$ with $u(V)\subseteq W$
([[def-continuous-map-top]]). It also satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Countable Choice selects the sequence of escape witnesses; the stated AC curve-calculus suppliers require both premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $p\in M$. Suppose that strong
causality fails at $p$ ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]

([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) $\sigma$ and parameters $s<t$ in

$$\sigma(s),\sigma(t)\in V,\qquad \sigma([s,t])\not\subseteq V .$$

and, for every $k\ge2$, points $x_k,y_k\in W$ with $x_k\to p$ and

$\sigma_k(0)=x_k$, $\sigma_k(1)=y_k$ and
$$\sigma_k([0,1])\not\subseteq W .$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian

$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

For each connected component $M_0\subseteq M$ and smooth Riemannian metric
$H$, let $d_H$ denote the Riemannian distance of $H|_{M_0}$. For the following absolutely continuous length assertion, also assume
Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), as required by the cited
fundamental theorem. For any locally
absolutely continuous curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M_0$, use the length

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such

$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space

The topology of $d_g$ is the manifold topology on every connected Riemannian manifold.
$d_g$ is a finite metric on a connected Riemannian manifold.

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves

$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for all sufficiently large $k$ for each fixed integer $n\ge1$ (for instance

**Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom
of Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).** Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]). Then the following five conditions are equivalent.

- **(a)** $(X,d)$ is compact ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
- **(b)** $(X,d)$ is countably compact ([[def-metric-compactness-variants]]).
- **(c)** $(X,d)$ is limit point compact.
- **(d)** $(X,d)$ is sequentially compact.
- **(e)** $(X,d)$ is complete ([[def-complete-metric-space]]) and totally bounded
  ([[def-totally-bounded]]).

**The two hypotheses are not needed everywhere, and the statement should not be
read as if they were.** Of the implications assembled below, all but two are
theorems of ZF. Dependent choice is used only for "sequentially compact implies
totally bounded" ([[thm-sequentially-compact-implies-totally-bounded]]), and
countable choice only for "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]). Each is an upper bound on
the cost of the proof given in this library and not a claim of necessity; the
implication-by-implication account is
[[rem-compactness-choice-ledger-metric]].

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]).

- An **open cover** of $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is a family
  $\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ of open sets with $X = \bigcup \mathcal{U}$,
  where $\bigcup \mathcal{U} = \{\, x \in X : x \in U \text{ for some } U \in \mathcal{U} \,\}$.
- A **subcover** of $\mathcal{U}$ is a subfamily $\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathcal{U}$
  that is itself an open cover.
- A family $\mathcal{V}$ of sets is **finite** when $\mathcal{V} = \varnothing$ or
  there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and sets $V_0, \dots, V_n$ with
  $\mathcal{V} = \{V_0, \dots, V_n\}$; repetitions in the list are allowed and
  harmless.
- $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is **compact** when every open cover of it has a finite
  subcover: for every open cover $\mathcal{U}$, either $X = \varnothing$ and the
  empty subfamily covers it, or there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and
  $U_0, \dots, U_n \in \mathcal{U}$ with
  $$X = U_0 \cup \dots \cup U_n .$$
- A subset $A \subseteq X$ is a **compact subset** of $X$ when the subspace
  $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ is a compact topological space, $\mathcal{T}_A$ being the
  subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

**Compactness of a subset is defined intrinsically, and only intrinsically.**
The last clause speaks about the subspace $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ and its own open
sets, not about families of open subsets of the ambient $X$. The two readings do
agree, but that is a theorem and not a convention: it is
[[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]], and no item of this library may use
the ambient reading without citing it. Taking the intrinsic reading makes
compactness a property of the topological space $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ alone.
Hence it is preserved when $A$ is embedded homeomorphically as a subspace, or
when another ambient space induces the same topology on $A$; it need not be
preserved if the induced topology changes. This is exactly the convention already fixed for
metric spaces by [[def-metric-compactness]], and the agreement of that
definition with this one is [[thm-compactness-agrees-with-metric-compactness]].

**The empty space is compact**, since the empty subfamily of any family covers
it; this is the reason the clause above is written with the two cases. Every
space listed as $\{x_0, \dots, x_n\}$ is compact too: given a cover, each $x_i$
lies in some member, and finitely many members named in this way already cover.
So every finite space is compact, whatever its topology, and in particular the
discrete topology on a finite set is compact while the discrete topology on an
infinite set is not ([[def-standard-topologies]]).

**The finiteness convention.** "Finite" above is the listing form. It agrees with
the definition of finiteness by equinumerosity with a natural number
([[def-countable]]), in both directions, and the agreement is the one already
discharged in [[def-metric-compactness]]: a nonempty set equinumerous with
$m \ge 1$ is listable, and a set listed as $\{a_0, \dots, a_n\}$ injects into
$\sigma(n)$ by sending $x$ to the least $i \le n$ with $a_i = x$. Neither
direction uses a choice principle; the second selects nothing, taking a least
index instead.

**Quasicompact is not used here.** Some authors, following Bourbaki, reserve
*compact* for a space that is both compact in the above sense and Hausdorff, and
call the open-cover condition alone *quasicompact*. This library follows the more
widely adopted convention: **compact** means the open-cover condition and nothing
more, and a Hausdorff hypothesis is always written out. The fork is recorded in
[[rem-compactness-conventions-and-choice-ledger]].

derivations.claim: (Preliminaries.) By [L1] there is no closed causal curve, $S$ is closed, and $M=I^-(S)\sqcup S\sqcup I^+(S)$. Consequently, for an inextendible future causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ we may speak of *the* parameter $t_0\in I$ with $\gamma(t_0)\in S$.

(The crossing property.) Let $\gamma:I	o M$ be an inextendible future causal curve and $t_0\in I$ with $\gamma(t_0)\in S$. Then $t>t_0$, $t\in I$ implies $\gamma(t)\in I^+(S)$, and $t<t_0$ implies $\gamma(t)\in I^-(S)$. Indeed, suppose $t>t_0$ and $\gamma(t)
otin I^+(S)$; by step 1.1 $\gamma(t)\in I^-(S)$ (it is not in $S$, as $t_0$ is the unique element of $\gamma^{-1}[S]$). Choose $s\in S$ with $\gamma(t)\ll s$. If $s=\gamma(t_0)$, the concatenation of the causal segment $\gamma|_{[t_0,t]}$ with a future timelike curve from $\gamma(t)$ to $\gamma(t_0)$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $\gamma(t_0)$ (nonconstant because $\gamma(t)\ll\gamma(t_0)$ forces $\gamma(t)
e\gamma(t_0)$), contradicting step 1.1. If $s
e\gamma(t_0)$, the same concatenation is a future causal curve from $\gamma(t_0)$ to $s$ with both endpoints in $S$; by [L2] it lies on an inextendible causal curve whose parameter set over $S$ therefore contains the two distinct parameters corresponding to $\gamma(t_0)$ and $s$, contradicting the Cauchy property. Hence $\gamma(t)\in I^+(S)$. The case $t<t_0$ is dual.

(The contradiction package from a closure relation.) Let $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a future-inextendible future causal curve and $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ a past-inextendible future causal curve such that for all $t_+\ge0$, $t_-\le0$ there are $u_k\le v_k$ with $u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$. Then this situation is impossible. Indeed, by [L2] there is an inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^+$ extending $\alpha^+$ with $\gamma^+|_{[0,\infty)}=\alpha^+$ and an inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^-$ whose restriction to $(-\infty,0]$ is $\alpha^-$. By the crossing property, step 2.1, there are $t_+'\in[0,\infty)$ with $\alpha^+(t_+')\in I^+(S)$ (take $t_+'$ larger than the unique $S$-parameter of $\gamma^+$ and than $0$) and $t_-'\le0$ with $\alpha^-(t_-')\in I^-(S)$. Choose $s_1\in S$ with $s_1\ll\alpha^+(t_+')$ and $s_2\in S$ with $\alpha^-(t_-')\ll s_2$. Let $u_k\le v_k$ be the corresponding sequences. Since $I^+(s_1)$ is open and contains $\alpha^+(t_+')$, for large $k$ we have $s_1\ll u_k$; since $I^-(s_2)$ is open and contains $\alpha^-(t_-')$, for large $k$ we have $v_k\ll s_2$. Fix such a $k$. Then $s_1\ll u_k\le v_k$, so $s_1\ll v_k$ by [L4]; and $s_1\ll v_k\ll s_2$, so $s_1\ll s_2$ by transitivity of $\ll$ [L4]. If $s_1\ne s_2$, this contradicts the acausality of $S$ [L1]. If $s_1=s_2=:s$, then the concatenation of a future timelike curve from $s$ to $u_k$, the future causal curve from $u_k$ to $v_k$ and a future timelike curve from $v_k$ to $s$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $s$ (nonconstant because $s\ll u_k$), contradicting step 1.1.

(The causal relation is closed.) Let $p_k\le q_k$ with $p_k\to p$ and $q_k\to q$. If infinitely many $p_k=q_k$, then $p=q$ (by uniqueness of limits) and $p\le q$. Otherwise, for large $k$ choose a future causal curve $\gamma_k$ with $\gamma_k(0')=p_k$, $\gamma_k(1')=q_k$ and reparametrize it by $h$-arclength: $\beta_k:[0,L_k]\to M$, $\beta_k(0)=p_k$, $\beta_k(L_k)=q_k$; the $L_k$ are positive. If the sequence $L_k$ is bounded, clause (i) of [L3] (applied to a subsequence with $L_k\to b$) gives a future causal curve $\beta:[0,b]\to M$ from $p$ to $q$, and either $b>0$ and $p\le q$ via $\beta$, or $b=0$, in which case $p=q$ by clause (i) and $p\le p$. If $L_k\to\infty$ along a subsequence, clause (ii) of [L3] gives future-inextendible $\alpha^+$ from $p$ and past-inextendible $\alpha^-$ to $q$ with the closure relation, which is impossible by step 3.1. Hence $p\le q$.

(Strong causality.) Suppose strong causality fails at $p\in M$ with neighbourhood $U$. By [L5] there are an open $W\ni p$ with $\overline W\subseteq U$ and future causal curves $\sigma_k:[0,1]\to M$ with endpoints $x_k,y_k\in W$, $x_k\to p$, $y_k\to p$, and $\sigma_k([0,1])\not\subseteq W$ for every $k$. Fix a coordinate ball $B=x^{-1}(B_{r_0})\subseteq W$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and let $c_1:=\sqrt c\,r_0/2>0$, where $c>0$ is a lower bound for the $h$-length density on the closed coordinate ball against the Euclidean coordinate speed ([[lem-local-comparison-of-a-riemannian-metric-with-the-euclidean-metric]], [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] clause (a)). For all sufficiently large $k$, $|x(x_k)|_{\mathrm e}<r_0/2$. The first exit point $w_k$ of $\sigma_k$ from $B$ then satisfies $|x(w_k)-x(x_k)|_{\mathrm e}\ge r_0-|x(x_k)|_{\mathrm e}>r_0/2$. The local metric lower bound and absolute-continuity calculus give $\ell_h(\sigma_k|_{[0,\tau_k]})\ge\sqrt c\int_0^{\tau_k}|(x\circ\sigma_k)'|_{\mathrm e}\,ds\ge\sqrt c\,|x(w_k)-x(x_k)|_{\mathrm e}>c_1$, where $\tau_k$ is the first-exit parameter. Reparametrize each $\sigma_k$ by $h$-arclength: $\alpha_k:[0,L_k]\to M$, with $\alpha_k(0)=x_k$, $\alpha_k(L_k)=y_k$; the same first-exit estimate gives $L_k\ge c_1$ for all large $k$. If $L_k$ is bounded along a subsequence, clauses (i) and (iii) of [L3] (with $x=z=p$ and $b=\lim L_k\ge c_1>0$) produce a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $p$, contradicting step 1.1. If $L_k\to\infty$, clause (ii) of [L3] produces the impossible configuration of step 3.1. Hence strong causality holds at every $p$.

(The causal diamonds are compact.) Let $p,q\in M$ and $A:=J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$; it is closed in $M$ because $J^+(p)$ and $J^-(q)$ are closed by step 4.1. With the metric $d_h$ inducing the manifold topology [L6], if $A$ were not compact then [L7] would give a sequence $r_k\in A$ with no convergent subsequence. For each $k$ choose a future causal curve from $p$ to $q$ through $r_k$ and reparametrize by $h$-arclength as $\gamma_k:[0,M_k]\to M$, with $\gamma_k(s_k)=r_k$. If $(M_k)$ is bounded, pass to $M_k\to b<\infty$. If $b=0$, then $d_h(r_k,p)\le M_k\to0$, contradiction. If $b>0$, clause (i) of [L3] gives the common-domain curves $\widetilde\gamma_k(t)=\gamma_k((M_k/b)t)$ converging uniformly on $[0,b]$ to $\gamma$. Put $t_k:=bs_k/M_k\in[0,b]$ and pass to a subsequence with $t_k\to t_*$. Then $r_k=\widetilde\gamma_k(t_k)\to\gamma(t_*)$ by uniform convergence and continuity, again a contradiction. Hence $M_k\to\infty$ along a subsequence, and clause (ii) of [L3] produces the impossible configuration of step 3.1. Therefore $A$ is compact.

(Conclusion.) Clause (a) is step 1.1, clause (b) is step 4.2, and clause (c) is step 5.1; strong causality and compactness of all causal diamonds are exactly the definition of global hyperbolicity in [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c).

boundaries.reason: The given Cauchy set must meet every inextendible curve in a nonempty spacetime; an empty diamond is nevertheless compact.

boundaries.evidence: Step 4.1 treats p=q and the b=0 limit by reflexivity, rather than producing a nonconstant curve of zero duration.
The exactly-one-parameter Cauchy condition is used in step 2.1 to exclude a second visit, even if an endpoint repeats the same S point.

boundaries.reason: The supplied Lorentz structure and positive-definite auxiliary metric exclude singular cone or length norms.

boundaries.evidence: Step 4.2 uses escape witnesses for the tail k>=2, with endpoints tending to p; no first witness index matters to the limit argument.

Statement boundary: Countable/Dependent Choice is explicitly assumed for witness curves, subsequence extraction and auxiliary calculus; the escaping-witness supplier supplies a nonempty countable family.

boundaries.reason: The theorem proves that a Cauchy set implies global hyperbolicity; it does not state the converse existence theorem.
Existence of a smooth Cauchy temporal splitting is supplied later, rather than proved as a reverse implication here.
