citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $u$ be a temporal function
on it in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (e), and write $\nabla u$ for its gradient. Then:

**(a)** $du(v)=g(\nabla u,v)>0$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$.

**(b)** For every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], the composite $u\circ\gamma$ is
locally absolutely continuous, its derivative satisfies
$(u\circ\gamma)'(t)>0$ at almost every $t\in I$, and consequently
$$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))\qquad\text{whenever }a<b\text{ and }\gamma \text{ is not constant on }[a,b].$$

**(c)** $u$ is a time function on $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (d); every level
set $u^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is achronal; and $(M,g,N)$ is causal and
chronological: it admits no nonconstant future causal curve with equal
endpoints.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas. Every compact parameter interval
admits a finite subdivision on each of whose pieces a chart representative
is absolutely continuous. For a continuous curve, the relative neighborhood
formulation and the compact chart-interval formulation of that definition
are equivalent.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into a finite-dimensional
smooth manifold $P$ (in particular $P=\mathbb R$) whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous in charts of $P$ using the same relative neighborhood definition,
and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (with the finite
admissible partition and one-sided endpoint convention of clause (a) of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. For $F:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$, the following are equivalent:

1. $F$ is absolutely continuous.
2. $F'$ exists almost everywhere, $F'\in L^1[a,b]$, and
$$F(x)-F(a)=\int_a^xF'(t)\,dt\quad\text{for every }x\in[a,b].$$

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $C\subseteq M$ be a strictly
convex normal set ([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]]
clause (b)), let $p\in C$, and write
$$W_p:=\exp_p^{-1}(C)\subseteq T_pM,\qquad v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q),\qquad P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q)),\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q)).$$
Define
$$J_C^+(p):=\{p\}\cup\{q\in C:\text{there is a future causal curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\},$$
so the reflexive endpoint $p$ is included even though a constant curve is
not in the curve class. Define
$$I_C^+(p):=\{q\in C:\text{there is a future timelike curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\}$$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Put
$$\mathcal C^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future causal or }v=0\},\quad \mathcal T^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future timelike}\},\quad \mathcal N^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future null and }v\ne0\}.$$
Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$, the position vector
$v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero for every $t\in[0,1]$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.**
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), let $p\in M$ and let $U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$
be a normal neighborhood of $p$ with $W_p$ star-shaped, as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ for $q\in U_p$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$, and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))$.

**(a) Differential in the second argument.** $D_p^2$ is smooth on $U_p$ and,
for every $q\in U_p$ and every $w\in T_qM$,
$$d(D_p^2)_q(w)=2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

**(b) Reversal.** Let $q\in U_p$ and let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$,
$\gamma(t)=\exp_p(t\,v(q))$, be the radial geodesic, so that
$\gamma(1)=q$. Then the reversed segment $t\mapsto\gamma(1-t)$ is the
restriction to $[0,1]$ of the maximal geodesic from $q$ with initial velocity
$-P(p,q)$; consequently
$$\exp_q^{-1}(p)=-P(p,q)\quad\text{and}\quad P(q,p)=-\,v(q)=-(\exp_p)^{-1}(q)$$
whenever the chosen normal inverse at $q$ has a domain containing
$-P(p,q)$. This condition holds in particular when both inverses are
those of one strictly convex normal set $C$ containing $p,q$ and the
inverse at $p$ used to define $v(q)$ is the one mapping $C$ to its
radial domain. Merely having $p,q\in C$ does not identify an independently
chosen inverse on $U_p$ with the inverse selected by $C$.
Under the inverse-domain condition, $D_q^2(p)=D_p^2(q)$ by the Gauss
lemma of [[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]].

**(c) Differential on pairs in a strictly convex normal set.** Use the inverse
domains selected by $C$ in this clause. If $C$ is a
strictly convex normal set ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in C$, then
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and for all $u\in T_pM$, $w\in T_qM$,
$$dD^2(p,q)(u,w)=2\,g_p\bigl(P(q,p),u\bigr)+2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix
$c>0$. All intervals $I,J$ below have nonempty interior. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve
   with $a<b$.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.
   For $a=b$, the unique section is its prescribed fibre vector and
   $P_\gamma$ is the identity; no $D_t$ condition is imposed on a singleton.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). For $w\in T_pM$ write
$h=h_n$ and $\gamma(w):=-g_p(n,w)$.

1. If $w$ is nonzero future causal, then $\gamma(w)>0$.
2. If $w$ is future unit timelike, then $\gamma(w)\ge1$, with
   $\gamma(w)=1$ if and only if $w=n$, and
   $g_p(h(w),h(w))=\gamma(w)^2-1$.
3. If $w$ is unit timelike, then $w$ is future-directed if and only if
   $g_p(n,w)<0$, and past-directed if and only if $g_p(n,w)>0$; in particular
   $g_p(n,w)\neq0$ for such $w$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis. Write
$v=v^0e_0+v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ for the coordinates of $v$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]) and

$$\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}.$$

Then $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert^2$, and the timelike set
$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$ satisfies

$$T=T_+\cup T_-,\qquad T_+:=\{v:v^0>\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad T_-:=\{v:v^0<-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\}.$$

The sets $T_+$ and $T_-$ are nonempty, disjoint, open in $V$ (for the metric
topology of the distance $d(u,w):=\lVert c(u)-c(w)\rVert_2$ induced by the
coordinates $c(v):=(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$), convex and path-connected, and they are
exactly the two connected components of $T$. In every $\eta$-orthonormal
ordered basis the two displayed coordinate sets coincide with the two
components of $T$ in some order, and they may be interchanged relative to a
previously fixed naming of the components. Moreover

$$\operatorname{cl}(T_+)=\{v:v^0\ge\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{v:v^0\le-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{0\}.$$

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(\overline{B_s})\times x^{-1}(\overline{B_s})\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$ with maximal flow $\Phi$, and let
$S\hookrightarrow M$ be an embedded codimension-one submanifold. If $X_p\notin T_pS$
for every $p\in S$, then there is an open neighbourhood
$\mathcal O\subseteq \mathbb R\times S$ of $\{0\}\times S$ such that the map

$$ F:\mathcal O\to M,\qquad F(t,p)=\Phi_t(p), $$

is an embedding. Its image is a flowout of $S$ along $X$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a continuous map,
where $I$ has its relative topology. A **chart representative** on a parameter
neighborhood $J\subseteq I$ is $x\circ\gamma|_J$, where $(U,x)$ is a smooth
chart and $\gamma(J)\subseteq U$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for each $t\in I$ there are
$\delta>0$ and a chart $(U,x)$ such that
$\gamma(I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta))\subseteq U$ and every coordinate of
$x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of
$I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta)$ in the sense of
[[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]. This includes one-sided neighborhoods
at included endpoints. Equivalently, for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the coordinates of $x\circ\gamma$ are
absolutely continuous on $[a,b]$. The equivalence and independence of the
chart and smooth atlas are proved in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]]
clause (a); continuity is part of both formulations.

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point: a
constant chart representative has derivative zero everywhere in its interior,
contradicting the full-measure nonzero-velocity requirement.

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ q\in J^+(p)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

derivations.claim: Since $\ker ds$ is spacelike, its one-dimensional Lorentz-orthogonal complement is timelike, and $\nabla s$ lies in that complement. Since $ds(\partial_s)=1$ and $\partial_s$ is future timelike, $\nabla s$ is past timelike. Thus [L1] gives strict increase of $s$ along every future causal curve. On any compact parameter interval $[t_1,t_2]$, (C2) and the absolutely continuous fundamental theorem give $|\sigma(\gamma(t_2))-\sigma(\gamma(t_1))|\le\int_{t_1}^{t_2}|(\sigma\circ\gamma)'|\le K\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(s\circ\gamma)'=K(s(\gamma(t_2))-s(\gamma(t_1)))$. Hence the curve image is the graph $(s,z(s))$ of a $K$-Lipschitz function on its time interval, without requiring a smooth inverse parameter map.

For the generic construction, the global smooth future timelike field $N$ is transverse to $\Sigma$, since no tangent vector to a spacelike hypersurface is timelike. By [L4] its flow $F(s,x)=\Phi_s^N(x)$ embeds an open zero-section neighborhood in $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ onto an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$. At $(0,x)$ the inverse time covector annihilates $T_x\Sigma$ and has value $1$ on $N_x$, so its gradient is past timelike. Shrink the flow domain to the open subset on which this remains true. Take all pairs $(V_j,a_j)$ with $V_j$ open in $\Sigma$, $a_j$ a positive rational, and $(-a_j,a_j)\times V_j$ contained in that temporal domain; their spatial sets cover $\Sigma$. A subordinate smooth locally finite partition $(\rho_j)$ exists by [L4]. Define $\delta(x)=\frac12\sum_j a_j\rho_j(x)$. This is smooth and positive. At each $x$ only finitely many terms are nonzero; one with maximal $a_j$ satisfies $x\in V_j$ and $\delta(x)\le a_j/2$. Hence the entire strip $|s|<\delta(x)$ lies in the temporal flow domain. Restricting $F$ to this strip gives the diffeomorphism and temporal coordinate stated in (d), with future timelike $F_*\partial_s=N$. Countable Choice is used for the flowout and partition suppliers; the causal calculus retains its stated Dependent Choice assumption.

The time graph is itself an admissible causal parametrization. At a differentiability point $s_0$ of this Lipschitz graph, choose fixed Euclidean coordinates and a positive-definite form $H_0$. For sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, the constant Lorentz form $g_0-\epsilon H_0$ has a closed convex future cone containing all future $g$-causal vectors based sufficiently near the limiting point: continuity makes $|(g-g_0)(v,v)|<\epsilon H_0(v,v)$ there, and orientation is fixed by the common temporal covector. The graph increment divided by its positive time increment is the integral of original causal velocities divided by that increment, so lies in this convex wider cone. Let the increment tend to zero and then $\epsilon\downarrow0$; the tangent $(1,z'(s_0))$ lies in the original future causal cone and is nonzero. This holds almost everywhere because the graph is Lipschitz. If it has a limit in $U$ at a finite time endpoint, adjoining that endpoint preserves the Lipschitz bound and the almost-everywhere causal tangent condition; hence it gives a causal segment from that endpoint to each interior point. The same reasoning holds in any relatively compact temporal coordinate box with a finite causal speed bound.

If $s(p)<0$, the past vertical fiber $(s',\sigma(p))$, $\inf I<s'\le s(p)$, avoids $S$ and has no limit in $U$ at its past end: a finite endpoint time is excluded from $I$, and an infinite endpoint has no finite coordinate limit. It is therefore past-inextendible in $U$, proving $p\notin D^+_U(S)$. Reversing time proves $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$, so (a) holds.

We record past heredity above the zero slice. If $r\in D^+_U(S)$ and $p\le_U r$ with $s(p)>0$, then $p\in D^+_U(S)$. Otherwise a past-inextendible avoiding curve through $p$, restricted to its past half ending at $p$, can be concatenated with a causal segment $p\to r$. Strict temporal increase keeps this segment at positive times, and finite concatenation preserves local absolute continuity and the causal tangent condition; its past end is unchanged. The resulting past-inextendible curve through $r$ avoids $S$, contradiction. The same argument works for any temporal collar whose zero slice is its initial hypersurface.

Around each $x\in\Sigma$ choose spatial coordinates $\sigma_i:V_i\to B_{R_i}$ and $a_i>0$ so that the closure of the product box $(-a_i,a_i)\times B_{R_i}$ lies in a larger temporal coordinate box inside the strip. This is possible by openness after shrinking a slice chart and its time interval. On each such compact enlarged box, the causal vectors normalized by $ds(v)=1$ have uniformly bounded spatial components. Indeed, an unbounded sequence, divided by its Euclidean norms and passed to a convergent subsequence over the compact box, would limit to a nonzero future causal vector annihilated by $ds$, impossible since $\ker ds$ is spacelike. Closedness follows from continuity of the metric and orientation. Thus there is $K_i\ge1$ with $|d\sigma_i(v)|\le K_i ds(v)$ throughout the local box. The corresponding intrinsic open funnels are $Q_i=F\{(s,x):x\in V_i,\ |s|<a_i,\ |\sigma_i(x)|+K_i|s|<R_i\}$. Their zero slices cover $\Sigma$. These constants are local; no common width, radius or speed constant is assumed.

Suppose a past-inextendible curve through $q$ with $s(q)>0$ avoids $S$. Its time values on the past half remain positive, and their infimum is $a\in[0,s(q))$. Its Lipschitz spatial graph has a limit $z_*$ in the closed Euclidean ball as $s\downarrow a$. Since $a\in I$, a limit with $|z_*|<R$ would be a limit point in $U$, contradicting inextendibility; hence $|z_*|=R$ and $R-|\sigma(q)|\le|z_*-\sigma(q)|\le K(s(q)-a)\le Ks(q)$. This is incompatible with the strict defining inequality of $Q$. The negative-time case reverses time, and zero-time points already lie on $S$. Thus $Q\subseteq D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$. It is open and contains every point $(0,\sigma)$ with $|\sigma|<R$, so is a neighborhood of the entire slice and satisfies $Q\subseteq W$.

If $q\in Q_i$ has positive time, a past-inextendible curve in $U_\Sigma$ through $q$ avoiding $\Sigma$ has only positive times. On the component of its past half remaining in the local box, the integrated speed estimate of step 1.1 holds with $K_i$. It cannot reach the spatial boundary at time $s\ge0$, since that would give $R_i-|\sigma_i(q)|\le K_i(s(q)-s)\le K_i s(q)$, contradicting the funnel inequality. It cannot exit through a time boundary while proceeding to the past with $0<s\le s(q)<a_i$. If it never exits, its spatial graph has a limit at its nonnegative past time infimum, and its norm is at most $|\sigma_i(q)|+K_i s(q)<R_i$. That endpoint lies in $U_\Sigma$, contradicting inextendibility there. Consequently $q\in D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)$. The negative case reverses time; zero-time points lie on $\Sigma$ already. Therefore $\bigcup_iQ_i\subset D_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)$, and $W_\Sigma$ contains the entire hypersurface. This proves the inclusion in the intrinsic domain of the whole collar, not merely in domains computed in individual boxes.

Let $\gamma$ be a two-sided inextendible causal curve in $W$ avoiding $S$. Its times are either entirely positive or entirely negative; assume positive. By (a), every image point belongs to $D^+_U(S)$. If its past end has no limit in $U$, its past half is already a past-inextendible avoiding curve in $U$, contradicting this membership. Otherwise it converges to $q\in U$ with $s(q)=a\ge0$. If $a=0$, then $q\in S\subseteq W$, contradicting inextendibility in $W$. It remains to exclude a positive-time endpoint $q$.

Suppose that endpoint has $s(q)>0$. Choose a small convex normal set $C\Subset U$ about $q$ and a point $r$ on a sufficiently short tail of $\gamma$ contained in $C$. Step 2.1 supplies a causal segment from $q$ to $r$, so $v=\exp_q^{-1}(r)$ is nonzero future causal by [L2]. Move $r$ a small positive distance along its future timelike coordinate fiber to $r_\epsilon\in C\cap W$. If $v$ is timelike, continuity keeps $\exp_q^{-1}(r_\epsilon)$ future timelike. If $v$ is null, its radial tangent $P(q,r)$ is nonzero future null, and the Gauss differential gives $\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}D_q^2(r_\epsilon)\right|_0=2g_r(P(q,r),\partial_s)<0$. Therefore $D_q^2(r_\epsilon)<0$ for small positive $\epsilon$, and future orientation persists because $v\ne0$. Thus in either case $q\ll_C r_\epsilon$. Smoothness of the two-point inverse and openness of the timelike cone give a neighborhood $V\subset C\cap\{s>0\}$ of $q$ such that $p\ll_C r_\epsilon$ for every $p\in V$. Since $r_\epsilon\in W$ has positive time, it belongs to $D^+_U(S)$ by (a), and step 2.3 gives $V\subset D^+_U(S)$. Hence $q\in W$, contradicting inextendibility in $W$. The negative case reverses time. Every inextendible $W$-curve therefore meets $S$, and strict temporal increase gives exactly one parameter visit. This proves (c)'s Cauchy property without asserting openness of a one-sided domain.

Negative-time vertical fibers of the variable strip avoid $\Sigma$ and have no limit in $U_\Sigma$ at their past endpoint $-\delta(x)$; the future counterparts handle positive times. Hence the intrinsic analogue of (a) holds. The heredity proof of step 2.3 applies on this temporal collar. An inextendible $W_\Sigma$-curve avoiding $\Sigma$ has one time sign; if its appropriate endpoint has no limit in $U_\Sigma$, the domain definition contradicts its membership. If the endpoint lies in $U_\Sigma$ at zero time, it is in $\Sigma\subset W_\Sigma$. If it lies at nonzero time, a relatively compact temporal chart around it has a finite speed bound by the normalization argument in step 2.4. Steps 2.1 and 5.1 then give the same local causal endpoint segment, radial timelike perturbation, and neighborhood forced into the appropriate one-sided domain by heredity. Thus that endpoint is in $W_\Sigma$, again contradiction. Every inextendible $W_\Sigma$-curve therefore meets $\Sigma$ exactly once. This argument also handles curves escaping spatially at infinity: they have no collar endpoint and are already quantified over by the intrinsic domain definition.

The hypersurfaces in (c),(d) are smooth spacelike embedded hypersurfaces and have the proved Cauchy intersection property. Applying [L5] to their respective induced open manifolds establishes both stated global-hyperbolicity consequences. Clauses (a),(b),(c),(d) follow respectively from steps 2.2, 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1, and 1.2, 2.4, 3.2 and 6.1.

boundaries.reason: The product chart contains the nonempty zero slice S; for an empty generic Sigma the collar/domain assertions have no points to construct or curves to intersect.

boundaries.evidence: The zero-time points lie on S. Step 3.1 treats them separately from positive and negative time, and R>0,K>=1 guard the collar margin.

boundaries.reason: The fixed spacetime dimension is four and the slices three; the theorem does not vary them to a one-dimensional ambient case.
The zero slice and generic Sigma are spacelike, making their time conormal timelike; a null initial hypersurface is excluded.

boundaries.evidence: Statement boundary: Steps 2.2 and 6.1 use vertical fibers ending at excluded collar boundary times, while steps 4.1-5.1 rule out an interior endpoint of a W-curve avoiding S.
Step 1.2 invokes Countable Choice for flowout and subordinate partition construction, and explicitly retains Dependent Choice for causal calculus; local delta has no asserted uniform lower bound.

boundaries.reason: The collar inclusion and Cauchy consequence are sufficient constructions under the chart hypotheses, with no iff assertion.
Global hyperbolicity of W does not claim that all ambient causal curves stay in the collar.

risk_review.notes: Checked temporal covector, AC time graph and wider-cone tangent limit; collar margin |sigma|+K|s|<R prevents avoiding curves reaching a spatial boundary. Past heredity plus radial timelike endpoint perturbation forces any finite nonzero-time endpoint into W. Generic noncompact flowout uses locally finite positive width delta and local compact cone bounds; all domains intrinsic. AC_omega/DC explicit; no global width or ambient acausality asserted.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous from the manifold topology to the usual topology of
$\mathbb R$: for every $p\in M$ and every open neighborhood $W$ of $u(p)$
there is an open neighborhood $V$ of $p$ with $u(V)\subseteq W$
([[def-continuous-map-top]]). It also satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a globally hyperbolic
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)) and let
$\mu$ be the finite volume measure of [[lem-gr-finite-smooth-volume-density]],
with $\mu(M)=1$, $\mu(O)>0$ for every nonempty open $O$ and $\mu(E)=0$ for
every chart-Lebesgue-null Borel set $E$. Then:

**(a)** for every sequence $p_k\to p$ in $M$, the indicator functions
$1_{I^-(p_k)}$ converge $\mu$-almost everywhere to $1_{I^-(p)}$, and
$$\mu\bigl(I^-(p_k)\bigr)\longrightarrow\mu\bigl(I^-(p)\bigr),$$
with the same statement for $I^+$;

**(b)** the maps $p\mapsto\mu(I^-(p))$ and $p\mapsto\mu(I^+(p))$ are
continuous on $M$;

**(c)** $J^-(p)=\overline{I^-(p)}$ and $\mu(J^-(p))=\mu(I^-(p))$ for every
$p$, and dually $J^+(p)=\overline{I^+(p)}$ and
$\mu(J^+(p))=\mu(I^+(p))$;

**(d)** if $p\ll q$ then
$$\mu\bigl(I^-(p)\bigr)<\mu\bigl(I^-(q)\bigr),\qquad \mu\bigl(I^+(p)\bigr)>\mu\bigl(I^+(q)\bigr).$$

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle beyond the stated assumptions is used.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ induced by the chart $\psi_p$ on $T_pM$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix
$c>0$. All intervals $I,J$ below have nonempty interior. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve
   with $a<b$.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.
   For $a=b$, the unique section is its prescribed fibre vector and
   $P_\gamma$ is the identity; no $D_t$ condition is imposed on a singleton.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a continuous map,
where $I$ has its relative topology. A **chart representative** on a parameter
neighborhood $J\subseteq I$ is $x\circ\gamma|_J$, where $(U,x)$ is a smooth
chart and $\gamma(J)\subseteq U$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for each $t\in I$ there are
$\delta>0$ and a chart $(U,x)$ such that
$\gamma(I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta))\subseteq U$ and every coordinate of
$x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of
$I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta)$ in the sense of
[[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]. This includes one-sided neighborhoods
at included endpoints. Equivalently, for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the coordinates of $x\circ\gamma$ are
absolutely continuous on $[a,b]$. The equivalence and independence of the
chart and smooth atlas are proved in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]]
clause (a); continuity is part of both formulations.

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point: a
constant chart representative has derivative zero everywhere in its interior,
contradicting the full-measure nonzero-velocity requirement.

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ q\in J^+(p)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous curve calculus and its fundamental theorem. Use the locally absolutely continuous Riemannian length of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a strongly causal time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(b)) and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite metric on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then for every compact set
$K\subseteq M$ there is $L(K)\in[0,\infty)$ such that
$$\ell_h(\gamma)\le L(K)$$
for every future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with $\gamma([a,b])\subseteq K$.

Consequently, if $\gamma$ is parametrized by $h$-arclength
($\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=t-s$) and its image is contained in the compact set
$K$, then $b-a\le L(K)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,

derivations.claim: (Well-definedness.) Let $p\in M$. The set $I^-(p)$ is open and nonempty (it contains the points $x^-_\varepsilon\ll p$ of [L4]), so $0<\mu(I^-(p))$ by positivity of the measure [L2]; and $\mu(I^-(p))<1$: the point $x^+_\varepsilon\gg p$ of [L4] does not lie in $J^-(p)$, because $x^+_\varepsilon\le p$ together with $p\ll x^+_\varepsilon$ would produce a nonconstant closed causal curve through $p$, contradicting [L1]; since $J^-(p)$ is closed by [L3] and $x^+_\varepsilon\notin J^-(p)$, a whole neighbourhood of $x^+_\varepsilon$ is disjoint from $I^-(p)$, so $\mu(I^-(p))\le1-\mu(\text{that neighbourhood})<1$. The same holds for $I^+(p)$. Hence $0<\mu(I^\pm(p))<1$ and $t(p)$ is a well-defined real number.

(Future decay of the future volumes.) Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be future-inextendible and fix $s_0\in I$. The family $\{I^+(\gamma(s))\}_{s\ge s_0}$ is decreasing, and each term has measure at most one. Suppose $\inf_{s\ge s_0}\mu(I^+(\gamma(s)))\ge\varepsilon>0$ for some $\varepsilon$. Choose an increasing cofinal sequence $s_j$ in the future parameter tail (a real interval admits one). The decreasing sequence $I^+(\gamma(s_j))$ has intersection $A:=\bigcap_{s\ge s_0}I^+(\gamma(s))$ by cofinality and nesting. Measure continuity from above [L7] gives $\mu(A)\ge\varepsilon$, so $A\ne\emptyset$; choose $z\in A$, so that $\gamma(s)\ll z$ for all $s\ge s_0$. Then $\gamma([s_0,\sup I))\subseteq J^+(\gamma(s_0))\cap J^-(z)$, a compact causal diamond, so by [L5] the $h$-length of every subcurve of $\gamma$ is at most $L(K)<\infty$ with $K:=J^+(\gamma(s_0))\cap J^-(z)$. Put $F(s)=\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s_0,s]})$ and $L_\infty=\sup_{s\ge s_0}F(s)\le L(K)$. Integral additivity gives $\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=F(t)-F(s)\le L_\infty-F(s)$ for $s<t$, which tends to zero as $s\to\sup I$. Hence [L6] makes the image points along an increasing cofinal parameter sequence Cauchy; they converge to $z_0$ by completeness. The same distance bound and cofinality show that the entire tail $\gamma(s)$ tends to $z_0$, contradicting future-inextendibility. No change of parametrization is needed. Therefore $\mu(I^+(\gamma(s)))\to0$ as $s\to\sup I$.

(Continuity.) If $p_k\to p$ then $\mu(I^\pm(p_k))\to\mu(I^\pm(p))$ by [L2], and the logarithm is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ by [L7]; the difference of two continuous functions is continuous, so $t$ is continuous. This proves (a).

(Strict monotonicity.) Let $p\le q$ with $p
e q$ and choose a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,1]	o M$ with $\gamma(0)=p$, $\gamma(1)=q$. Fix $s_0\in(0,1)$ and put $x:=\gamma(s_0)$; then $p\le x\le q$, and $p
e x$, $x
e q$ because equality would give a nonconstant closed causal subcurve, contrary to [L1]. We show $\mu(I^-(q))>\mu(I^-(p))$ and $\mu(I^+(p))>\mu(I^+(q))$. For the first: $I^-(p)\subseteq I^-(q)$, since $y\ll p\le q$ gives $y\ll q$ by [L2]. If $I^-(q)$ were contained in $J^-(p)$, then for every point $x^-_\varepsilon\ll x$ of [L4] we would have $x^-_\varepsilon\ll x\le q$, hence $x^-_\varepsilon\ll q$ and therefore $x^-_\varepsilon\in I^-(q)\subseteq J^-(p)$, that is, $x^-_\varepsilon\le p$; letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and using closedness of $\le$ [L3] gives $x\le p$, which with $p\le x$ yields a nonconstant closed causal curve through $x$ (nonconstant because $p
e x$), contradicting [L1]. Hence $I^-(q)\setminus J^-(p)$ is nonempty; it is open (as the intersection of the open $I^-(q)$ with the complement of the closed $J^-(p)$) and is contained in $I^-(q)\setminus I^-(p)$, so it has positive $\mu$-measure, and additivity gives $\mu(I^-(q))\ge\mu(I^-(p))+\mu(I^-(q)\setminus J^-(p))>\mu(I^-(p))$. For the second: $I^+(q)\subseteq I^+(p)$ by the dual push-up, and if $I^+(p)\subseteq J^+(q)$ then every $x^+_\varepsilon\gg x$ satisfies $x^+_\varepsilon\gg x\ge p$, hence $x^+_\varepsilon\gg p$ and $x^+_\varepsilon\in I^+(p)\subseteq J^+(q)$, that is $x^+_\varepsilon\ge q$; closedness of $\le$ gives $x\ge q$, which with $x\le q$ is again a closed causal curve, contradicting [L1]. So $I^+(p)\setminus J^+(q)$ is a nonempty open subset of $I^+(p)\setminus I^+(q)$ and $\mu(I^+(p))>\mu(I^+(q))$. Since $L$ is strictly increasing, $t(p)=L(\mu(I^-(p)))-L(\mu(I^+(p)))<L(\mu(I^-(q)))-L(\mu(I^+(q)))=t(q)$. This proves (b).

(Future growth of the past volumes and the limit at the future end.) With $\gamma$, $s_0$ as in step 1.2: for $s\ge s_0$ one has $I^-(\gamma(s_0))\subseteq I^-(\gamma(s))$ because $y\ll\gamma(s_0)\le\gamma(s)$ gives $y\ll\gamma(s)$ by [L2], hence $\mu(I^-(\gamma(s)))\ge c:=\mu(I^-(\gamma(s_0)))>0$ by monotonicity and step 1.1. Combining with step 1.2, $$t(\gamma(s))=L\bigl(\mu(I^-(\gamma(s)))\bigr)-L\bigl(\mu(I^+(\gamma(s)))\bigr)\ge L(c)-L\bigl(\mu(I^+(\gamma(s)))\bigr).$$ Since $\mu(I^+(\gamma(s)))\to0+$ and the logarithm tends to $-\infty$ at $0+$ [L7], the second term satisfies $-L(\mu(I^+(\gamma(s))))\to+\infty$, while $L(\mu(I^-(\gamma(s))))\ge L(c)$ remains bounded below; hence $t(\gamma(s))\to+\infty$ as $s\to\sup I$.

(The limit at the past end.) Apply steps 1.2 and 2.3 in the time-reversed orientation: the time reverse of $\gamma$ is future-inextendible, its future volumes are the $I^-$-volumes of $\gamma$, and its past volumes the $I^+$-volumes; hence $\mu(I^-(\gamma(s)))\to0$ as $s\to\inf I$ and, with $\mu(I^+(\gamma(s)))\ge\mu(I^+(\gamma(s_1)))>0$ for $s\le s_1$, one gets $t(\gamma(s))\to-\infty$ as $s\to\inf I$. This proves (c) for future-directed curves; a past-directed inextendible causal curve becomes future-directed after reversing its parameter, and the limits are interchanged accordingly.

(Level sets are Cauchy.) Let $c\in\mathbb R$ and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be inextendible and causal; reversing the parameter if necessary, assume it is future-directed. By step 2.3 and step 3.1 the continuous function $s\mapsto t(\gamma(s))$ on the interval $I$ tends to $+\infty$ at $\sup I$ and to $-\infty$ at $\inf I$; since the intermediate value theorem [L7] applies to continuous real functions on connected domains, for every $c$ between the two limits there is $s\in I$ with $t(\gamma(s))=c$. Hence every level set is met at least once. It is met at most once: if $s_1<s_2$ with $t(\gamma(s_1))=t(\gamma(s_2))=c$, then $\gamma(s_1)\le\gamma(s_2)$ with $\gamma(s_1)\ne\gamma(s_2)$ (equality would be a nonconstant closed causal curve on $[s_1,s_2]$, contradicting [L1]), so strict monotonicity, step 2.2, gives $t(\gamma(s_1))<t(\gamma(s_2))$, a contradiction. Therefore every inextendible causal curve meets $t^{-1}(c)$ in exactly one parameter value, so $t^{-1}(c)$ is a Cauchy set; acausality is the special case of two points $y\le y'$ of the level set with $y\ne y'$, which strict monotonicity forbids. This proves (d).

boundaries.reason: The chronological past and future of each p are nonempty open sets by short timelike segments; their measures therefore support the logarithms.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 proves 0<mu(I-plus/minus(p))<1 before logarithms or the quotient are taken; zero-volume boundaries do not enter these denominators.
Each inextendible curve has exactly one parameter at each level by strict increase plus the intermediate value argument in step 4.1.

boundaries.reason: The measure has total mass one and is positive on opens; the zero measure is excluded, while null causal directions remain admissible.

boundaries.evidence: Statement boundary: Steps 1.2,2.3 and 3.1 take endpoint limits of volumes, giving plus/minus infinite time along inextendible curves without claiming finite endpoint values.
Statement boundary: The specified Countable/Dependent Choice premises cover the curve and compactness suppliers; the cofinal sequence is chosen inside the one given real parameter interval.

boundaries.reason: Continuity, monotonicity, divergence and Cauchy levels are properties of the defined volume time, not an iff definition of global hyperbolicity.
An arbitrary function with Cauchy levels is not identified with this logarithmic volume formula.

risk_review.notes: Checked positive volumes below one, continuity of logs, finite-volume continuity from above and a common compact diamond forcing finite tail h-length and an endpoint limit. Strict increase across distinct causal events uses a positive open-set gap and no-loop causality; both time infinities and IVT give exactly one level visit. Nonconstant return is excluded by causality, not merely velocity. AC_omega/DC explicit.

([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)); in

every inextendible causal curve.
